docs.title: 11.9.1. lib/state/session.dart
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/state/session.dart - WHO is logged in?
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The logged-in user (or null), in a ChangeNotifier provided to the whole
// application (provider, see example 20): readable by the screens AND by
// the router, which listens to it to re-evaluate its guards (refreshListenable).
//
// The JWT token itself is NOT here: it is in a cookie (handled by the
// browser on the web, by CookieClient on the phone). The
// session only keeps the DESCRIPTION of the user ({ login, name, role }).
//
// When the application starts, the session is empty: check() asks
// the server, only once, who is logged in (GET /api/auth/me).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';

import '../api/rdvmedecins_api.dart';
import '../api/types.dart';

class Session extends ChangeNotifier {
  final RdvMedecinsApi _api;
  User? _user;
  // true after a WANTED logout (button, account deletion); false
  // after an expired session. The router takes it into account (see router.dart)
  bool _voluntaryLogout = false;
  // has the question "who is logged in?" already been asked to the server?
  Future<void>? _checking;

  Session(this._api);

  User? get user => _user;
  bool get voluntaryLogout => _voluntaryLogout;

  // only asks the server the first time (the Future is kept)
  Future<void> check() => _checking ??= _api.me().then(
    (u) => _change(u),
    onError: (Object _) => _change(null), // 401: nobody; or server unreachable
  );

  Future<void> logIn(String login, String password, String captchaId, String captcha) async {
    _change(await _api.logIn(login, password, captchaId, captcha));
  }

  // the user has changed their name or login (PUT /api/my-account)
  void update(User u) => _change(u);

  Future<void> logOut() async {
    try {
      await _api.logOut();
    } finally {
      forget(voluntary: true);
    }
  }

  // without asking the server anything: session expired, account deleted
  void forget({bool voluntary = false}) => _change(null, voluntary: voluntary);

  // notifyListeners: the router (refreshListenable) re-evaluates its guards, and
  // leaves on its own a screen that the new user is not allowed to see
  void _change(User? u, {bool voluntary = false}) {
    _user = u;
    _voluntaryLogout = voluntary;
    notifyListeners();
  }
}

// what we deduce from the user: extensions ("getters" added to User?)
extension Rights on User? {
  bool get isAdmin => this?.role == Role.admin;
  bool get isPatient => this?.role == Role.user;
  // ADMIN and DOCTOR: book and cancel the appointments of any patient
  bool get isManager => this?.role == Role.admin || this?.role == Role.doctor;
  // the home page of each role, just after logging in
  String get homePage => isPatient ? '/my-area' : '/schedule';
}

Who is logged in? The session stores the user's DESCRIPTION (login, name, role), not the token, which remains in the user's cookie.

  • Lines 36–38: The question “Who is logged in?” is sent to the server ([GET /api/auth/me]) only ONCE, at startup: [??=] only assigns the [Future] if [_checking] is [null]. Subsequent calls return the same [Future], which has already been completed: the router can call [check()] before each navigation at no cost. At startup, if the stored cookie contains a token that is still valid, the user remains logged in;
  • lines 41–42: the connection: if the server refuses, [_api.logIn] throws an [ApiError], and [_change] is not called;
  • lines 48–52: logout: the user is forgotten even if the server does not respond ([finally]);
  • lines 61–64: all changes go through here, and notify the listeners: the screens displaying the user (the layout), the cache (which is cleared), and the router (which reevaluates its guards). [_voluntaryLogout] distinguishes between an intentional logout and an expired session (see [router.dart]);
  • lines 69–75: an extension adds getters to an existing type, in this case [User?]: [session.user.isAdmin] is [false] if no one is logged in, without first checking for [null] ([this?.role]).

docs.title: 11.9.2. lib/state/messages.dart
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/state/messages.dart - the messages displayed to the user
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Same presentation as the other RdvMedecins clients:
//   - a SUCCESS is displayed at the TOP of the screen (green banner);
//   - an ERROR at the BOTTOM (pink banner), always visible.
// A message is a translation KEY (+ its parameters): it is therefore
// translated again on its own if the user changes the language.
//
// The "flash" messages: an action that ends with a change of
// screen (booking, adding a doctor...) leaves its message with
// flash(); it will be displayed on the NEXT screen, then disappear at the
// following navigation. It is the router that calls newPage() at the
// end of each navigation (see router.dart).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';

import '../api/api_error.dart';

typedef Message = ({String key, Map<String, String> params});

class Messages extends ChangeNotifier {
  Message? success;
  Message? error;
  // the messages to display on the next screen
  Message? _pendingSuccess;
  Message? _pendingError;

  void showSuccess(String key, [Map<String, String> params = const {}]) {
    success = (key: key, params: params);
    error = null;
    notifyListeners();
  }

  void showError(String key, [Map<String, String> params = const {}]) {
    error = (key: key, params: params);
    success = null;
    notifyListeners();
  }

  // an ApiError -> the message of the screen; any other error is a
  // bug of the client, which we let propagate
  void showApiError(Object e) {
    if (e is! ApiError) throw e;
    showError(e.key, e.params);
  }

  void clear() {
    success = null;
    error = null;
    notifyListeners();
  }

  // for the NEXT screen
  void flash({bool success = true, required String key, Map<String, String> params = const {}}) {
    if (success) {
      _pendingSuccess = (key: key, params: params);
    } else {
      _pendingError = (key: key, params: params);
    }
  }

  // a new screen: the messages of the previous one disappear, the flash
  // messages appear
  void newPage() {
    success = _pendingSuccess;
    error = _pendingError;
    _pendingSuccess = null;
    _pendingError = null;
    notifyListeners();
  }
}

Application messages: a success message at the top of the screen, an error message at the bottom (see [layout.dart]).

  • Line 21: A message is a translation KEY and its parameters (a single record). It is translated only when displayed: changing the language re-translates the displayed messages;
  • Lines 44–46: An [ApiError] becomes the screen’s error message. Any other exception is a client-side issue: we re-throw it so that it appears in the console during development, rather than hiding it;
  • lines 56–60: a message for the NEXT screen: an action that ends with a screen change (a reservation, an addition, etc.) places its message here;
  • lines 66–71: called every time the address changes (see [main.dart]): messages from the previous screen disappear, and flash messages appear.

docs.title: 11.9.3. lib/state/cache.dart
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/state/cache.dart - the data already read from the server
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The list of doctors almost never changes: no need to read it again at
// each visit of the schedule. The cache keeps the Future of each read,
// under a KEY ('doctors', 'schedule/1/2026-10-05'...):
//
//     cache.read('doctors', () => api.list(PersonType.doctors))
//
// returns the Future already kept, or starts the read and keeps it.
// After a change, we INVALIDATE the keys concerned (they will be
// read again at the next request): cache.invalidate('schedule').
// A failed read is not kept: the next one will try again.
// The cache is a ChangeNotifier: invalidate() notifies its listeners. A
// screen still alive (even hidden under another one in the stack, like
// the schedule under its booking dialog) can thus read its data again.
// This is, in a few lines, what the TanStack Query library of the
// React client does.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';

class Cache extends ChangeNotifier {
  final Map<String, Future<Object?>> _futures = {};

  Future<T> read<T>(String key, Future<T> Function() load) {
    final future = _futures.putIfAbsent(key, () {
      final f = load();
      // on failure, we forget this Future (the next request will try again)
      f.then((_) {}, onError: (Object _) => _futures.remove(key));
      return f;
    });
    return future.then((v) => v as T);
  }

  // forgets all the keys that start with prefix, and notifies the screens
  void invalidate(String prefix) {
    _futures.removeWhere((key, _) => key.startsWith(prefix));
    notifyListeners();
  }

  // change of user: we forget everything, WITHOUT notifying (the screens of
  // the previous user are going to disappear, they must not read anything again)
  void clear() => _futures.clear();
}

Data already read from the server: the equivalent, in a few lines, of [TanStack Query] in the [React] client.

  • Line 24: The cache stores [Future], not actual values: two screens requesting the same data while it is in transit receive the SAME [Future], and only a single request is sent;
  • Lines 26–33: A generic method: [read<List<Person>>(...)] returns a [Future<List<Person>>] (the type [T] is most often inferred from the function [load]). [putIfAbsent]: the value of the key, or, if the key is missing, the result of the function, stored under that key. A failed read is ignored: the next request will try again;
  • lines 37–39: After a modification, the affected keys are discarded, and the screens are notified. The calendar screen listens for this: after a reservation, it reloads itself, even if hidden behind the reservation window;
  • line 44: when the user changes, everything is cleared without notifying anyone: the previous user’s screens will disappear; they have nothing to reload.

docs.title: 11.10.1. lib/formatting.dart
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/formatting.dart - the display of times and days
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The server sends RAW data (startHour: 8, startMinute: 0; day:
// "2026-10-05"); the formatting, which depends on the language, is the business
// of the client (see example 09).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:intl/intl.dart';

import 'api/types.dart';

String _twoDigits(int n) => n.toString().padLeft(2, '0');

// "8:05" rather than "8:5"
String time(int h, int m) => '$h:${_twoDigits(m)}';

// "8:00 - 8:20"
String timeRange(Slot s) => '${time(s.startHour, s.startMinute)} - ${time(s.endHour, s.endMinute)}';

// a date -> "yyyy-MM-dd" (the format of the API)
String toDay(DateTime d) => '${d.year}-${_twoDigits(d.month)}-${_twoDigits(d.day)}';

String today() => toDay(DateTime.now());

// true if day is a date that exists, in the yyyy-MM-dd format
bool isValidDate(String day) {
  if (!RegExp(r'^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$').hasMatch(day)) return false;
  final d = DateTime.tryParse(day);
  return d != null && toDay(d) == day; // 2026-02-30 -> 2026-03-02: refused
}

// "Monday, October 5, 2026" / "lundi 5 octobre 2026"
String longDate(String day, String language) => DateFormat.yMMMMEEEEd(language).format(DateTime.parse(day));

Formatting the raw data from the server (see example 09):

  • line 22: a [DateTime] in the API format (“2026-10-05”);
  • lines 27–30: Is the date in the address valid? [DateTime.tryParse] accepts “2026-02-30” (March 2): we verify that the same string is present;
  • line 34: “Monday, October 5, 2026” or “lundi 5 octobre 2026,” depending on the language ([DateFormat.yMMMMEEEEd] derived from [intl]).

docs.title: 11.11.1. lib/router.dart
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/router.dart - the screens of the application and their access rights
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The SAME addresses as the other clients (/login, /schedule, /doctors,
// /my-area...). On the web, they are displayed in the address bar;
// on the phone, they remain invisible, but organize the application
// just as much (and the stack of screens of the Back button).
//
// All the screens are in a ShellRoute, whose widget, AppLayout, displays
// them between the top bar and the error panel.
//
// The GUARDS: the redirect function of the GoRouter is called before EACH
// navigation. It can be asynchronous: the first time (startup of
// the application, F5 on the web), it waits for the server's answer to the
// question "who is logged in?" (session.check()). Then it checks the
// rights of the requested screen (rightsOf), and redirects if needed.
// REMINDER: these checks are only a CONVENIENCE (not displaying a useless
// screen). The protection of the data is ensured by the server, which
// checks the token and the role again with EACH request.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';

import 'api/rdvmedecins_api.dart';
import 'api/types.dart';
import 'state/messages.dart';
import 'state/session.dart';
import 'pages/schedule.dart';
import 'pages/login.dart';
import 'pages/patient_area.dart';
import 'pages/register.dart';
import 'pages/my_account.dart';
import 'pages/error_page.dart';
import 'pages/person_form.dart';
import 'pages/persons.dart';
import 'widgets/layout.dart';

// the access rights of a screen: public (without login), or reserved to
// some roles (null: all logged-in roles)
typedef Rights = ({bool public, Set<Role>? roles});

Rights rightsOf(String path) => switch (path) {
  '/login' || '/register' => (public: true, roles: null),
  _ when path.startsWith('/doctors') || path.startsWith('/clients') => (public: false, roles: {Role.admin}),
  '/my-area' || '/my-account' => (public: false, roles: {Role.user}),
  '/schedule' || '/forbidden' || '/' => (public: false, roles: null),
  _ => (public: true, roles: null), // unknown address: the 404 page, for everyone
};

// only an INTERNAL path ("/doctors"): never "//other-site.com"
String? internalPath(String? r) => r != null && r.startsWith('/') && !r.startsWith('//') ? r : null;

// "3" -> 3; "", "abc", "-2", missing (null) -> null
int? positiveInteger(String? value) {
  final n = int.tryParse(value ?? '');
  return n != null && n > 0 ? n : null;
}

GoRouter createRouter(Session session, Messages messages, RdvMedecinsApi api) {
  // the three management screens of the doctors OR of the clients (ADMIN)
  List<GoRoute> personRoutes(PersonType type) => [
    GoRoute(
      path: '/${type.name}',
      builder: (_, _) => PersonsPage(type: type),
    ),
    GoRoute(
      path: '/${type.name}/add',
      builder: (_, _) => PersonFormPage(type: type),
    ),
    GoRoute(
      path: '/${type.name}/:id/edit',
      builder: (_, state) {
        final id = positiveInteger(state.pathParameters['id']);
        // /doctors/abc/edit: this address does not exist
        return id == null ? const ErrorPage(code: 404) : PersonFormPage(type: type, id: id);
      },
    ),
  ];

  return GoRouter(
    initialLocation: '/login',
    // the session changes (login, logout, expiry): the guards
    // are re-evaluated for the current screen
    refreshListenable: session,
    redirect: (context, state) async {
      await session.check();
      final user = session.user;
      final path = state.uri.path;
      final rights = rightsOf(path);
      if (rights.public) {
        // logged in: the login screen no longer makes sense. It is HERE that we
        // leave it, just after logging in: the session has changed, the router
        // (which listens to it) re-evaluates its guards. We go to the screen requested before
        // the login (?redirect=...), otherwise to the home page of the role
        if (path == '/login' && user != null) {
          return internalPath(state.uri.queryParameters['redirect']) ?? user.homePage;
        }
        return null;
      }
      if (user == null) {
        // wanted logout: the login screen, quite simply
        if (session.voluntaryLogout) return '/login';
        // expired session, address opened without being logged in: we remember
        // the requested screen, to come back to it after logging in
        return Uri(path: '/login', queryParameters: {'redirect': state.uri.toString()}).toString();
      }
      if (path == '/') return user.homePage;
      if (rights.roles != null && !rights.roles!.contains(user.role)) return '/forbidden';
      return null;
    },
    routes: [
      ShellRoute(
        builder: (context, state, child) => AppLayout(child: child),
        routes: [
          GoRoute(path: '/', builder: (_, _) => const ErrorPage(code: 404)), // (redirected above)
          GoRoute(
            path: '/login',
            builder: (_, state) {
              // the login of the address: 30 characters at most
              final login = state.uri.queryParameters['login'] ?? '';
              return LoginPage(login: login.length > 30 ? login.substring(0, 30) : login);
            },
          ),
          GoRoute(
            path: '/schedule',
            builder: (_, state) => SchedulePage(
              doctorId: positiveInteger(state.uri.queryParameters['doctorId']),
              day: state.uri.queryParameters['day'],
              book: positiveInteger(state.uri.queryParameters['book']),
            ),
          ),
          ...personRoutes(PersonType.doctors),
          ...personRoutes(PersonType.clients),
          GoRoute(
            path: '/register',
            // a guard SPECIFIC to this route: without a pass (captcha
            // solved on the login screen), back to the login screen
            redirect: (context, state) async {
              final valid = await api.registrationAccessStatus().catchError((_) => false);
              if (valid) return null;
              messages.flash(success: false, key: 'ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT');
              return '/login';
            },
            builder: (_, _) => const RegisterPage(),
          ),
          GoRoute(path: '/my-area', builder: (_, _) => const PatientAreaPage()),
          GoRoute(path: '/my-account', builder: (_, _) => const MyAccountPage()),
          GoRoute(path: '/forbidden', builder: (_, _) => const ErrorPage(code: 403)),
        ],
      ),
    ],
    // an address that no route describes: the 404 page, in the layout
    errorBuilder: (context, state) => const AppLayout(child: ErrorPage(code: 404)),
  );
}

The application screens, their addresses, and their access rights (see examples 17 and 18).

  • Line 40: a screen’s access rights: public, or restricted to certain roles ([null]: all roles);
  • Lines 42–47: the permissions for each address; in ONE place only: a [switch] string expression. ['/login' || '/register']: an “or” pattern; [_ when ...]: an “anything” pattern, with a condition (a guard);
  • line 51: the address [?redirect=] is only followed if it is a INTERNAL path: on the web, an address [/login?redirect=//pirate-site.com] sent by email must not take the user elsewhere after they log in;
  • lines 54–56: The parameters of an address are strings, written by anyone (on the web): “abc” or “-2” become [null];
  • lines 61–78: a local function that generates the three routes for the doctors OR the clients: [/doctors], [/doctors/add], [/doctors/:id/edit]. [:id]: a path parameter, read by [state.pathParameters['id']];
  • line 81: the initial screen on the phone (on the web, this is the address entered);
  • line 84: the router monitors the session: with each change (connection, disconnection, expiration), it reevaluates its guards for the current screen and switches screens if necessary;
  • lines 85–109: THE guard, called before each navigation:
    • line 86: the first time, we wait for the server’s response to the question “who is logged in?”; after that, this call costs nothing;
    • lines 90–98: A public screen is accessible to everyone; however, a logged-in user has no business being on the login screen: they go to the screen they requested before logging in, or to the home screen for their role. This is how the application exits the login screen after a successful login: the login screen itself does not need to navigate;
    • lines 100–105: No one is logged in: proceed to the login screen. After a session has expired, or if a protected URL (on the web) was opened directly, the requested screen ([?redirect=]) is retained so that the user can return to it after logging in; after an intentional logout, it is not retained;
    • lines 107–108: [/] leads to the role’s home page; an insufficient role leads to a 403 page;
  • lines 112–113: All screens are displayed within the layout (the top bar, the menu, the messages);
  • lines 117–121: [/login?login=jbernard] (after creating an account) pre-fills the login field;
  • lines 125–129: the three calendar parameters, read from the URL; the entire screen state is present there (see [schedule.dart]);
  • lines 135–142: a guard SPECIFIC to a route: account creation requires a pass, which the server issues once the CAPTCHA has been entered ([POST /api/register/access], see login screen). Without it, you are redirected to the login screen with a message;
  • line 153: an address not mapped to any route: the 404 page, in the layout.

These safeguards are merely a formality: they prevent a useless screen from being displayed. Data protection is ensured by the server, which re-verifies the token and role with every request.

docs.title: 11.12.1. lib/widgets/layout.dart
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/widgets/layout.dart - the LAYOUT common to all the screens
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The widget of the router's ShellRoute (see router.dart):
//   - the top bar: title, language (FR / EN), logout;
//   - the side menu ("drawer", Drawer), opened by the ☰ button: the
//     screens allowed to the user's role. "Doctors" and "Patients"
//     only appear for the ADMIN: a mere display convenience, the
//     real protection being that of the server;
//   - a success message at the TOP;
//   - the current screen (child);
//   - the error panel at the BOTTOM.
// On a large screen (web, tablet), the menu is displayed permanently
// on the left: a NavigationRail instead of the drawer.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';

import '../state/messages.dart';
import '../state/session.dart';
import '../i18n/translations.dart';

// a menu entry: path, key of the label, icon
typedef MenuEntry = ({String path, String key, IconData icon});

List<MenuEntry> menuEntries(Session session) {
  final u = session.user;
  if (u == null) return const [];
  return [
    if (u.isPatient) (path: '/my-area', key: 'APP.MENU_MY_AREA', icon: Icons.home),
    (path: '/schedule', key: 'APP.MENU_SCHEDULE', icon: Icons.calendar_month),
    if (u.isAdmin) ...[
      (path: '/doctors', key: 'APP.MENU_DOCTORS', icon: Icons.medical_services),
      (path: '/clients', key: 'APP.MENU_PATIENTS', icon: Icons.people),
    ],
    if (u.isPatient) (path: '/my-account', key: 'APP.MENU_ACCOUNT', icon: Icons.manage_accounts),
  ];
}

class AppLayout extends StatelessWidget {
  final Widget child;

  const AppLayout({super.key, required this.child});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final translations = context.watch<Translations>();
    final t = translations.t;
    final session = context.watch<Session>();
    final u = session.user;
    final entries = menuEntries(session);
    // the current address, as the router knows it
    final path = GoRouter.of(context).routerDelegate.currentConfiguration.uri.path;
    final active = entries.indexWhere((e) => path.startsWith(e.path));
    // MediaQuery: the dimensions of the screen; from 800 points on, a large screen
    final largeScreen = MediaQuery.sizeOf(context).width >= 800;

    // the session becomes empty; the router, which listens to it, displays the login screen
    Future<void> logOut() => session.logOut().catchError((_) {}); // even if the server does not respond

    final content = Column(
      crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch,
      children: [
        const _SuccessMessage(),
        Expanded(child: child),
        const _ErrorPanel(),
      ],
    );

    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(
        title: Text(t('APP.TITLE')),
        backgroundColor: Theme.of(context).colorScheme.primary,
        foregroundColor: Theme.of(context).colorScheme.onPrimary,
        actions: [
          // FR / EN: no request to the server, the screen is translated again on the spot
          PopupMenuButton<String>(
            tooltip: t('APP.LANGUAGE'),
            // the text, in the colour of the bar's icons (onPrimary)
            icon: Text(
              translations.language.toUpperCase(),
              style: TextStyle(fontWeight: FontWeight.bold, color: Theme.of(context).colorScheme.onPrimary),
            ),
            onSelected: translations.changeLanguage,
            itemBuilder: (_) => [for (final l in languages) PopupMenuItem(value: l, child: Text(l.toUpperCase()))],
          ),
          if (u != null) IconButton(tooltip: t('APP.LOGOUT'), icon: const Icon(Icons.logout), onPressed: logOut),
        ],
      ),
      // the drawer: only when logged in, and only on a small screen
      drawer: u == null || largeScreen
          ? null
          : NavigationDrawer(
              selectedIndex: active < 0 ? null : active,
              onDestinationSelected: (i) {
                Navigator.pop(context); // closes the drawer
                context.go(entries[i].path);
              },
              children: [
                // the header: who is logged in
                Padding(
                  padding: const EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(28, 16, 16, 10),
                  child: Column(
                    crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
                    children: [
                      Text(u.name, style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleMedium),
                      Chip(label: Text(u.role.name.toUpperCase())),
                    ],
                  ),
                ),
                for (final e in entries) NavigationDrawerDestination(icon: Icon(e.icon), label: Text(t(e.key))),
              ],
            ),
      body: u == null || !largeScreen
          ? content
          : Row(
              children: [
                NavigationRail(
                  selectedIndex: active < 0 ? null : active,
                  labelType: NavigationRailLabelType.all,
                  onDestinationSelected: (i) => context.go(entries[i].path),
                  destinations: [
                    for (final e in entries) NavigationRailDestination(icon: Icon(e.icon), label: Text(t(e.key))),
                  ],
                ),
                const VerticalDivider(width: 1),
                Expanded(child: content),
              ],
            ),
    );
  }
}

// the success message, at the top
class _SuccessMessage extends StatelessWidget {
  const _SuccessMessage();

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final success = context.watch<Messages>().success;
    if (success == null) return const SizedBox.shrink();
    final t = context.watch<Translations>().t;
    return Material(
      color: Colors.green.shade50,
      child: ListTile(
        leading: Icon(Icons.check_circle, color: Colors.green.shade700),
        title: Text(t(success.key, success.params), style: TextStyle(color: Colors.green.shade900)),
        trailing: IconButton(icon: const Icon(Icons.close), onPressed: context.read<Messages>().clear),
      ),
    );
  }
}

// the error panel, at the bottom: always visible, even if the screen scrolls
class _ErrorPanel extends StatelessWidget {
  const _ErrorPanel();

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final error = context.watch<Messages>().error;
    if (error == null) return const SizedBox.shrink();
    final t = context.watch<Translations>().t;
    return Material(
      color: const Color(0xFFF8D7DA),
      // SafeArea: above the phone's navigation bar
      child: SafeArea(
        top: false,
        child: ListTile(
          leading: Icon(Icons.error, color: Colors.red.shade800),
          title: Text(t(error.key, error.params), style: TextStyle(color: Colors.red.shade900)),
          trailing: IconButton(icon: const Icon(Icons.close), onPressed: context.read<Messages>().clear),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}

The layout, the widget of the [ShellRoute]: the element that surrounds all screens.

  • Line 26: a menu entry: a record;
  • lines 28–38: entries permitted for the user’s role, via an [if] in a list (example 03). [...[...]]: the spread operator inserts multiple elements at once;
  • line 55: the current address, to mark the active menu entry;
  • line 58: the screen width, in points. Above 800 points (the web, a tablet in landscape mode), the menu will be displayed permanently;
  • line 61: logout—the session is cleared, and the router, which is listening for this, displays the login screen. [catchError]: even if the server does not respond, the user is considered logged out;
  • lines 63–68: the success message at the top, the screen in the middle ([Expanded]: all remaining space), the error at the bottom;
  • lines 73–89: the top bar: the title, the language menu ([PopupMenuButton]: a button that opens a list; its icon here is text, “FR” or “EN”), the logout button;
  • lines 93–113: on a small screen, a drawer ([NavigationDrawer]), which opens via the ☰ button that [Scaffold] automatically adds to the top bar. Tapping an entry closes the drawer ([Navigator.pop]) and changes the URL;
  • Lines 116–129: On a large screen, a [NavigationRail]: the menu, arranged in a column to the left of the content;
  • lines 137–154: the success message. [context.watch<Messages>()]: the widget is rebuilt every time the messages change; when there are no messages, it takes up no space ([SizedBox.shrink]);
  • lines 168–169: the error area is at the bottom of the screen: [SafeArea] keeps it separate from the phone’s navigation bar (the buttons or gesture bar of [Android]).

docs.title: 11.12.3. lib/widgets/form_submit.dart
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/widgets/form_submit.dart - sending a form to the server
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// All the forms of the application follow the same pattern as
// example 25: no rule is checked on the phone (they live
// in ONE place only, the server), and in case of refusal:
//   - the error of each field (ApiError.fields) is displayed under the field;
//   - the general message (ApiError.key) is displayed at the bottom of the screen.
// This class groups these steps (it is the Command of example 23,
// completed with the errors of the fields). A screen creates one per form:
//
//     final _submit = FormSubmit(messages);
//     if (await _submit.submit(() => api.register(input))) { ... }
//     InputField(..., error: _submit.errors['lastName'])
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';

import '../api/api_error.dart';
import '../state/messages.dart';

class FormSubmit extends ChangeNotifier {
  final Messages _messages;
  // the error of each field: a translation KEY
  Map<String, String> errors = {};
  // the parameters of the error messages ({{min}}...), sent back by the server
  Map<String, String> params = {};
  bool submitting = false;

  FormSubmit(this._messages);

  // runs the submission; returns true if it succeeded. On an ApiError, the
  // errors are displayed and we return false
  Future<bool> submit(Future<void> Function() action) async {
    if (submitting) return false; // no double submission
    errors = {};
    params = {};
    submitting = true;
    notifyListeners();
    try {
      await action();
      return true;
    } on ApiError catch (e) {
      _messages.showApiError(e);
      errors = e.fields;
      params = e.params;
      return false;
    } finally {
      submitting = false;
      notifyListeners();
    }
  }

  // the user changes a field: its error disappears
  void clearError(String field) {
    if (errors.containsKey(field)) {
      errors = {...errors}..remove(field);
      notifyListeners();
    }
  }
}

Submitting a form to the server: the [Command] from Example 23, supplemented with field errors (Example 25).

  • Lines 34–50: Submission: no duplicate submissions; during submission, [submitting] (the buttons are disabled); on an [ApiError], the general message at the bottom of the screen and the error for each field are displayed. [finally] runs in all cases, even after a [return];
  • lines 55–57: the user corrects a field; the error disappears. We replace the [Map] with a copy, rather than modifying it: the old one may have been provided by the server ([e.fields]), and a constant [Map] ([const {}]) does not change.

docs.title: 11.12.4. lib/widgets/input_field.dart
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/widgets/input_field.dart - a complete form field
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Label + field + help message OR error message. All the
// forms of the application use it:
//
//   InputField(label: 'PERSONS.LASTNAME_LABEL', maxLength: 20,
//              value: _input['lastName'], onChanged: (v) => _edit('lastName', v),
//              error: _submit.errors['lastName'])
//
// It is a CONTROLLED widget (see example 11): the value belongs to the
// parent form; didUpdateWidget copies into the field a value that
// the parent has changed itself. label, help and error are translation
// KEYS; params, the parameters of their messages ({{min}}...).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';

import '../i18n/translations.dart';

class InputField extends StatefulWidget {
  final String label;
  final String value;
  final ValueChanged<String> onChanged;
  final String? error;
  final String? help;
  final Map<String, String> params;
  final bool secret; // a password: hidden characters
  final int? maxLength;
  final bool autofocus;
  final Iterable<String>? autofill; // for the phone's password manager

  const InputField({
    super.key,
    required this.label,
    required this.value,
    required this.onChanged,
    this.error,
    this.help,
    this.params = const {},
    this.secret = false,
    this.maxLength,
    this.autofocus = false,
    this.autofill,
  });

  @override
  State<InputField> createState() => _InputFieldState();
}

class _InputFieldState extends State<InputField> {
  late final _controller = TextEditingController(text: widget.value);

  @override
  void didUpdateWidget(InputField old) {
    super.didUpdateWidget(old);
    if (widget.value != _controller.text) _controller.text = widget.value;
  }

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _controller.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final t = context.watch<Translations>().t;
    final error = widget.error;
    return Padding(
      padding: const EdgeInsets.only(bottom: 8),
      child: TextField(
        controller: _controller,
        obscureText: widget.secret,
        autocorrect: !widget.secret,
        autofocus: widget.autofocus,
        maxLength: widget.maxLength,
        autofillHints: widget.autofill,
        decoration: InputDecoration(
          labelText: t(widget.label),
          errorText: error == null ? null : t(error, widget.params),
          helperText: widget.help == null ? null : t(widget.help!, widget.params),
          helperMaxLines: 2,
          errorMaxLines: 3,
          counterText: '', // no "0/20" counter under the field
        ),
        onChanged: widget.onChanged,
      ),
    );
  }
}

A complete form field: label, field, help text, or error message. All forms use this.

  • lines 22–32: the parameters. The label, help text, and error message are translation KEYS;
  • lines 53–58: a controlled widget (Example 11): the value belongs to the parent. If the parent changes it itself (the CAPTCHA cleared after a failure), [didUpdateWidget] copies it back into the field;
  • lines 75–79: a password is masked, and the spell checker does not interfere; [autofillHints] tells the phone’s password manager what the field contains (a username, a password, a new password);
  • lines 80–86: the label, the error message (which replaces the help text), and the help text. [maxLength] limits the input and would display a counter (“3/20”) below the field; [counterText: ''] hides it.

// =========================================================================
// lib/widgets/person_fields.dart - title, first name, last name
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The identity fields, common to three forms: the ADMIN's doctor / client
// form, "Create a patient account" and "Manage my account". The parent
// passes it the values, the errors, and the function that changes a field:
//     PersonFields(values: _input, errors: _submit.errors, onChanged: _edit)
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';

import '../i18n/translations.dart';
import 'input_field.dart';

const titles = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];

class PersonFields extends StatelessWidget {
  final Map<String, Object?> values;
  final Map<String, String> errors;
  final void Function(String field, String value) onChanged;

  const PersonFields({super.key, required this.values, required this.errors, required this.onChanged});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final t = context.watch<Translations>().t;
    final titleError = errors['title'];
    return Column(
      crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch,
      children: [
        // DropdownButtonFormField: a drop-down list with label and error
        DropdownButtonFormField<String>(
          // key: if the value is changed by the code, the field is re-created with it
          key: ValueKey(values['title']),
          initialValue: values['title'] as String,
          decoration: InputDecoration(
            labelText: t('PERSONS.TITLE_LABEL'),
            errorText: titleError == null ? null : t(titleError),
          ),
          items: [for (final title in titles) DropdownMenuItem(value: title, child: Text(title))],
          onChanged: (title) => onChanged('title', title!),
        ),
        const SizedBox(height: 8),
        InputField(
          label: 'PERSONS.FIRSTNAME_LABEL',
          maxLength: 20,
          value: values['firstName'] as String,
          onChanged: (v) => onChanged('firstName', v),
          error: errors['firstName'],
        ),
        InputField(
          label: 'PERSONS.LASTNAME_LABEL',
          maxLength: 20,
          value: values['lastName'] as String,
          onChanged: (v) => onChanged('lastName', v),
          error: errors['lastName'],
        ),
      ],
    );
  }
}

The identity fields (title, first name, last name), common to the ADMIN forms, the account creation form, and the “Manage my account” form.

  • Line 21: The parent passes the values, the errors, and ONE function to modify any field;
  • Lines 33–42: The title, in a drop-down list, with label and error message, like an input field. [initialValue] is read only when the field is created; the key ([ValueKey]) recreates it if the value changes via code.

The CAPTCHA image, the “Another image” button, and the field. The widget does not call the server: the login screen requests the image because it needs its identifier to send the response.

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/widgets/confirmation.dart - "Are you sure?"
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Taken from example 16. The message is a translation KEY:
//     if (await confirm(context, 'SCHEDULE.CANCEL_CONFIRM')) { ... }
// "No, go back" rather than "Cancel": the question is sometimes "Cancel this
// appointment?", and a "Cancel" button would be ambiguous there. The focus is on
// "No": an absent-minded press on Enter deletes nothing.
// A new question clears the messages of the previous action.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';

import '../state/messages.dart';
import '../i18n/translations.dart';

Future<bool> confirm(BuildContext context, String key) async {
  context.read<Messages>().clear();
  final t = context.read<Translations>().t;
  final yes = await showDialog<bool>(
    context: context,
    builder: (context) => AlertDialog(
      title: Text(t('CONFIRMATION.TITLE')),
      content: Text(t(key)),
      actions: [
        TextButton(autofocus: true, onPressed: () => Navigator.pop(context, false), child: Text(t('CONFIRMATION.NO'))),
        FilledButton(
          style: FilledButton.styleFrom(backgroundColor: Colors.red.shade700),
          onPressed: () => Navigator.pop(context, true),
          child: Text(t('CONFIRMATION.YES')),
        ),
      ],
    ),
  );
  return yes ?? false;
}

The confirmation window from Example 16, translated: [if (await confirm(context, 'SCHEDULE.CANCEL_CONFIRM')) ...]. The focus is on “No” ([autofocus]): on the web, accidentally pressing Enter does not delete anything.

docs.title: 11.12.8. lib/widgets/booking_dialog.dart
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/widgets/booking_dialog.dart - the booking dialog of a slot
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A window above the schedule, grey background included. It is NOT
// opened by showDialog: it is part of the schedule screen, which
// displays it when its ADDRESS asks for it (/schedule?...&book=7, see
// pages/schedule.dart). The address thus describes the whole screen, dialog included.
//
// The widget does not talk to the server: it calls
//   - onConfirm, with the chosen patient (null for a patient who books
//     for themselves);
//   - onClose.
// It is the schedule screen that decides what to do with them.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';

import '../api/types.dart';
import '../i18n/translations.dart';

class BookingDialog extends StatefulWidget {
  final String time; // "8:00 - 8:20"
  final List<Person> clients; // ADMIN / DOCTOR: the patients to choose from
  final String? patient; // USER: the patient is the user themselves
  final bool submitting;
  final ValueChanged<int?> onConfirm;
  final VoidCallback onClose;

  const BookingDialog({
    super.key,
    required this.time,
    required this.clients,
    required this.patient,
    required this.submitting,
    required this.onConfirm,
    required this.onClose,
  });

  @override
  State<BookingDialog> createState() => _BookingDialogState();
}

class _BookingDialogState extends State<BookingDialog> {
  int? _clientId;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final t = context.watch<Translations>().t;
    final patient = widget.patient;
    return Stack(
      children: [
        // ModalBarrier: the grey background; touching it closes the dialog
        ModalBarrier(color: Colors.black54, onDismiss: widget.onClose),
        Center(
          child: Card(
            margin: const EdgeInsets.all(24),
            child: Padding(
              padding: const EdgeInsets.all(20),
              child: Column(
                mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
                crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch,
                children: [
                  Text(t('BOOKING_DIALOG.TITLE'), style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleLarge),
                  const SizedBox(height: 12),
                  Text(t('BOOKING_DIALOG.SLOT', {'time': widget.time})),
                  const SizedBox(height: 12),
                  // a patient books for themselves: no list (and the server
                  // would ignore a possible clientId anyway)
                  if (patient != null)
                    Text.rich(
                      TextSpan(
                        children: [
                          TextSpan(text: '${t('BOOKING_DIALOG.PATIENT_LABEL')}: '),
                          TextSpan(
                            text: patient,
                            style: const TextStyle(fontWeight: FontWeight.bold),
                          ),
                        ],
                      ),
                    )
                  else
                    DropdownButtonFormField<int?>(
                      initialValue: _clientId,
                      isExpanded: true,
                      decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: t('BOOKING_DIALOG.PATIENT_LABEL')),
                      items: [
                        DropdownMenuItem(value: null, child: Text(t('BOOKING_DIALOG.CHOOSE_PATIENT'))),
                        for (final c in widget.clients) DropdownMenuItem(value: c.id, child: Text(c.label)),
                      ],
                      onChanged: (id) => setState(() => _clientId = id),
                    ),
                  const SizedBox(height: 20),
                  // OverflowBar: the buttons side by side, one under the other if they do not fit
                  OverflowBar(
                    alignment: MainAxisAlignment.end,
                    spacing: 8,
                    children: [
                      TextButton(onPressed: widget.onClose, child: Text(t('BOOKING_DIALOG.CANCEL'))),
                      FilledButton(
                        onPressed: widget.submitting ? null : () => widget.onConfirm(_clientId),
                        child: Text(t('BOOKING_DIALOG.CONFIRM')),
                      ),
                    ],
                  ),
                ],
              ),
            ),
          ),
        ),
      ],
    );
  }
}

The slot reservation window. It is NOT opened by [showDialog]: it is part of the calendar screen, which displays it when its address requests it ([&book=7]).

  • Lines 23–28: The widget does not communicate with the server; it receives the data it displays, along with two functions called to confirm (with the selected patient) or close;
  • lines 51–54: A [Stack] overlays its children: first, a [ModalBarrier]—with a grayed-out background—that covers the entire screen and blocks taps intended for the calendar (tapping closes the window), followed by the window itself, centered;
  • lines 70–91: A patient makes a reservation for themselves: their name, without a list. Either the ADMIN or the doctor selects the patient from a drop-down list; the selection determines the window’s state;
  • lines 95–102: the buttons ([OverflowBar]: side by side, or one below the other if they don’t fit); “Confirm” is disabled during submission.

docs.title: 11.13.1. lib/pages/login.dart
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/pages/login.dart - the login screen (/login)
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Same screen as in the other clients: login, password, captcha, and
// a second button "Create a patient account" which checks the SAME captcha
// before opening the account creation.
//
// /login?login=jbernard: the login field is pre-filled (just after the
// creation of an account).
// After a successful login, this screen does NOT navigate by itself: the
// session changes, and it is the router that leaves the login screen
// (to /login?redirect=... or the home page of the role, see router.dart).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';

import '../api/rdvmedecins_api.dart';
import '../api/types.dart';
import '../state/messages.dart';
import '../state/session.dart';
import '../i18n/translations.dart';
import '../widgets/captcha_field.dart';
import '../widgets/input_field.dart';
import '../widgets/form_submit.dart';
import '../widgets/page_title.dart';

class LoginPage extends StatefulWidget {
  final String login; // the login of the address (?login=...)

  const LoginPage({super.key, this.login = ''});

  @override
  State<LoginPage> createState() => _LoginPageState();
}

class _LoginPageState extends State<LoginPage> {
  late final _api = context.read<RdvMedecinsApi>();
  late final _messages = context.read<Messages>();
  late final _submit = FormSubmit(_messages);
  late final Map<String, String> _input = {'login': widget.login, 'password': '', 'captcha': ''};
  Captcha? _captcha;

  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
    _reloadCaptcha();
  }

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _submit.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  // a new image: it is needed after EACH attempt, because an image can only
  // be used ONCE (the server forgets it as soon as it has checked it)
  Future<void> _reloadCaptcha() async {
    Captcha? captcha;
    try {
      captcha = await _api.captcha();
    } catch (_) {
      captcha = null; // server unreachable: the login will fail with a clear message
    }
    if (mounted) setState(() => _captcha = captcha);
  }

  void _edit(String field, String value) {
    setState(() => _input[field] = value);
    _submit.clearError(field);
  }

  // the two buttons share this flow: sending, then, on failure,
  // error message and a NEW image
  Future<void> _attempt(Future<void> Function() action) async {
    _messages.clear();
    final succeeded = await _submit.submit(action);
    if (!succeeded && mounted) {
      setState(() => _input['captcha'] = '');
      await _reloadCaptcha();
    }
  }

  // on success, nothing else to do here: the router changes the screen
  Future<void> _logIn() => _attempt(
    () => context.read<Session>().logIn(
      _input['login']!.trim(),
      _input['password']!,
      _captcha?.id ?? '',
      _input['captcha']!,
    ),
  );

  Future<void> _createAccount() => _attempt(() async {
    await _api.registrationAccess(_captcha?.id ?? '', _input['captcha']!);
    if (mounted) context.go('/register');
  });

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final t = context.watch<Translations>().t;
    return PageTitle(
      titleKey: 'LOGIN.TITLE',
      child: ListenableBuilder(
        listenable: _submit,
        builder: (context, _) => ListView(
          padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
          children: [
            Text(t('LOGIN.TITLE'), style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.headlineSmall),
            const SizedBox(height: 12),
            // AutofillGroup: the phone's password manager can fill in the form
            AutofillGroup(
              child: Column(
                children: [
                  InputField(
                    label: 'LOGIN.LOGIN_LABEL',
                    value: _input['login']!,
                    onChanged: (v) => _edit('login', v),
                    error: _submit.errors['login'],
                    autofill: const [AutofillHints.username],
                  ),
                  InputField(
                    label: 'LOGIN.PASSWORD_LABEL',
                    secret: true,
                    value: _input['password']!,
                    onChanged: (v) => _edit('password', v),
                    error: _submit.errors['password'],
                    autofill: const [AutofillHints.password],
                  ),
                ],
              ),
            ),
            CaptchaField(
              svg: _captcha?.svg,
              value: _input['captcha']!,
              onChanged: (v) => _edit('captcha', v),
              onReload: _reloadCaptcha,
              error: _submit.errors['captcha'],
            ),
            const SizedBox(height: 8),
            FilledButton(onPressed: _submit.submitting ? null : _logIn, child: Text(t('LOGIN.SUBMIT'))),
            const SizedBox(height: 12),
            OutlinedButton(onPressed: _submit.submitting ? null : _createAccount, child: Text(t('LOGIN.CREATE_ACCOUNT'))),
            Padding(
              padding: const EdgeInsets.only(top: 4),
              child: Text(
                t('LOGIN.CREATE_ACCOUNT_HELP'),
                textAlign: TextAlign.center,
                style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.bodySmall,
              ),
            ),
            const SizedBox(height: 16),
            _DemoAccounts(t: t),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}

// the demo accounts
