  • lines 152–157: a list item with a checkbox. [controlAffinity] places the checkbox on the left. [onChanged] receives the new value of the checkbox, of type [bool?] (a checkbox can have a third state, “undetermined”): [!] indicates that it is not [null];
  • line 160: the label’s style depends on the task: struck through and gray if it’s done, the default style ([null]) otherwise;
  • lines 163–165: a “trash can” button. The anonymous function [() => _remove(t, 'button')] allows arguments to be passed: the task on this line;
  • Lines 171–174: [GestureDetector] makes any widget responsive to gestures: tap ([onTap], [onTapDown]...), double-tap, long press, swipe, pinch... Here, a simple colored box ([Container]) responds to three gestures;
  • lines 175–178: [Container] is a box, specifying margin, background, border, size, and alignment. [decoration] describes its background: a color, rounded corners. [Color(0xFFE7F5FF)]: a color specified by its code ARGB (opacity FF, then red, green, blue);
  • line 184: the log.

Add a task, check the second one, tap the bottom area; then drag the first task to the left (to the middle while dragging; to the right once the line is removed):

In [React], the browser events ([click], [keydown]...) are the same for all elements; in [Flutter], each interactive widget declares its own, with typed parameters ([onPressed], [onChanged], [onSubmitted]...), and [GestureDetector] adds gestures to those that do not have any. The editor, which knows the parameters for each widget, suggests them as you type.

docs.title: 3.5. Example 05: All Field Types
docs.text:
This example uses the form from Example 05 of course [React], with the input fields from [Flutter]: text boxes, radio buttons, checkboxes, drop-down lists, bulleted lists, sliders, and calendars.

// =========================================================================
// lib/ex05_controlled_fields/main.dart - all the types of fields
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A CONTROLLED field displays a value of the state and notifies the widget of
// each change (onChanged), which updates the state: the state is the
// single source of truth. Modifying the state (from the code) modifies the field.
// What onChanged passes depends on the field:
//   - TextField (with a controller)    -> the text (String);
//   - Checkbox, Switch                 -> bool? / bool;
//   - Radio (in a RadioGroup)          -> the value of the chosen button;
//   - DropdownButton                   -> the value of the chosen item;
//   - FilterChip                       -> bool: is the chip selected?
//   - Slider                           -> double;
//   - showDatePicker (a dialog)        -> a Future<DateTime?>.
// The TextField is a special case: it keeps its text in a
// TextEditingController, which we create, read (controller.text),
// modify... and release (dispose).
// Same form as example 05 of the React course; everything happens on the
// phone, without a server.
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter_localizations/flutter_localizations.dart';

const titles = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];
const hobbies = ['sport', 'music', 'reading', 'cinema'];
const countries = {'fr': 'France', 'be': 'Belgium', 'ch': 'Switzerland'};
const languages = {'fr': 'French', 'en': 'English', 'es': 'Spanish'};

void main() {
  runApp(
    MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      // the texts of Flutter itself (calendar, OK / CANCEL buttons) in
      // English (see example 21)
      locale: const Locale('en'),
      supportedLocales: const [Locale('en'), Locale('fr')],
      localizationsDelegates: GlobalMaterialLocalizations.delegates,
      home: const FormPage(),
    ),
  );
}

class FormPage extends StatefulWidget {
  const FormPage({super.key});

  @override
  State<FormPage> createState() => _FormPageState();
}

class _FormPageState extends State<FormPage> {
  // one state per field of the form
  String _title = 'Mme';
  final _name = TextEditingController();
  final _age = TextEditingController(text: '30');
  String _presentation = '';
  bool _newsletter = false;
  final Set<String> _hobbies = {'reading'}; // a SET: no duplicates
  String _country = 'fr';
  final Set<String> _languages = {};
  DateTime? _birthDate; // null: not chosen yet
  double _satisfaction = 3;
  String? _sent;

  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
    // a controller NOTIFIES its listeners on each change of the text:
    // the screen is redrawn (the model displayed live)
    _name.addListener(_redraw);
    _age.addListener(_redraw);
  }

  void _redraw() => setState(() {});

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _name.dispose();
    _age.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  // "2026-10-05": the date format of the RdvMedecins API
  String? get _birthDateText => _birthDate?.toIso8601String().substring(0, 10);

  // all the values, gathered into one object (what would be sent to a server)
  Map<String, Object?> get _model => {
    'title': _title,
    'name': _name.text.trim(),
    'age': int.tryParse(_age.text), // null if the field is empty
    'presentation': _presentation,
    'newsletter': _newsletter,
    'hobbies': _hobbies.toList(),
    'country': _country,
    'languages': _languages.toList(),
    'birthDate': _birthDateText,
    'satisfaction': _satisfaction.round(),
  };

  // the date of birth: a calendar dialog. showDatePicker returns
  // a Future, the chosen date (or null: dialog closed without a choice)
  Future<void> _chooseBirthDate() async {
    final choice = await showDatePicker(
      context: context,
      initialDate: _birthDate ?? DateTime(2000, 1, 1),
      firstDate: DateTime(1900),
      lastDate: DateTime.now(),
    );
    if (choice != null) {
      setState(() => _birthDate = choice);
    }
  }

  // the state modified BY THE CODE: the fields follow
  void _example() {
    setState(() {
      _title = 'Mr';
      _name.text = 'MARTIN';
      _age.text = '42';
      _hobbies
        ..clear()
        ..addAll(['sport', 'cinema']);
      _country = 'be';
    });
  }

  void _send() {
    // JsonEncoder.withIndent: indented JSON; jsonEncode: on one line
    setState(() => _sent = jsonEncode(_model));
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final titleStyle = Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleSmall;
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Example 05 - the controlled fields')),
      body: ListView(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
        children: [
          Text('Title', style: titleStyle),
          // RadioGroup: the chosen value (groupValue) and the function called
          // when one of the Radio buttons it contains is chosen
          RadioGroup<String>(
            groupValue: _title,
            onChanged: (value) => setState(() => _title = value!),
            child: Row(
              children: [
                for (final t in titles) ...[Radio<String>(value: t), Text(t), const SizedBox(width: 12)],
              ],
            ),
          ),
          Row(
            children: [
              Expanded(
                flex: 2,
                child: TextField(
                  controller: _name,
                  decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'Name'),
                ),
              ),
              const SizedBox(width: 12),
              Expanded(
                child: TextField(
                  controller: _age,
                  decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'Age'),
                  keyboardType: TextInputType.number,
                ),
              ),
            ],
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 8),
          // Focus: notifies when its child GAINS or LOSES the focus. The field
          // is not linked to the state on each keystroke: its text is only read when
          // leaving the field (like onBlur in HTML)
          Focus(
            onFocusChange: (hasFocus) {
              if (!hasFocus) setState(() {});
            },
            child: TextFormField(
              initialValue: _presentation,
              maxLines: 2,
              decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'Presentation (updated when leaving the field)'),
              onChanged: (text) => _presentation = text, // WITHOUT setState: nothing is redrawn
            ),
          ),
          // a single box: true / false
          CheckboxListTile(
            contentPadding: EdgeInsets.zero,
            controlAffinity: ListTileControlAffinity.leading,
            title: const Text('Receive the newsletter'),
            value: _newsletter,
            onChanged: (checked) => setState(() => _newsletter = checked!),
          ),
          Text('Hobbies', style: titleStyle),
          // several chips for ONE set: the value is added or removed
          Wrap(
            spacing: 8,
            children: [
              for (final l in hobbies)
                FilterChip(
                  label: Text(l),
                  selected: _hobbies.contains(l),
                  onSelected: (selected) => setState(() => selected ? _hobbies.add(l) : _hobbies.remove(l)),
                ),
            ],
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 8),
          Row(
            children: [
              Text('Country', style: titleStyle),
              const SizedBox(width: 16),
              // a drop-down list: value tells which item is chosen
              DropdownButton<String>(
                value: _country,
                items: [
                  for (final MapEntry(key: code, value: name) in countries.entries)
                    DropdownMenuItem(value: code, child: Text(name)),
                ],
                onChanged: (code) => setState(() => _country = code!),
              ),
            ],
          ),
          Text('Spoken languages', style: titleStyle),
          Wrap(
            spacing: 8,
            children: [
              for (final MapEntry(key: code, value: name) in languages.entries)
                FilterChip(
                  label: Text(name),
                  selected: _languages.contains(code),
                  onSelected: (selected) => setState(() => selected ? _languages.add(code) : _languages.remove(code)),
                ),
            ],
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 8),
          Row(
            children: [
              Text('Satisfaction: ${_satisfaction.round()} / 5', style: titleStyle),
              Expanded(
                // a slider: 5 notches, from 1 to 5
                child: Slider(
                  value: _satisfaction,
                  min: 1,
                  max: 5,
                  divisions: 4,
                  onChanged: (v) => setState(() => _satisfaction = v),
                ),
              ),
            ],
          ),
          ListTile(
            contentPadding: EdgeInsets.zero,
            leading: const Icon(Icons.cake),
            title: const Text('Date of birth'),
            subtitle: Text(_birthDateText ?? 'not chosen'),
            trailing: OutlinedButton(onPressed: _chooseBirthDate, child: const Text('Choose')),
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 8),
          // Wrap: the buttons wrap to the next line on a narrow screen
          Wrap(
            spacing: 8,
            runSpacing: 8,
            children: [
              FilledButton(onPressed: _send, child: const Text('Send')),
              OutlinedButton(onPressed: _example, child: const Text('Fill from the code')),
            ],
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 16),
          Text('The model, live', style: titleStyle),
          Container(
            padding: const EdgeInsets.all(8),
            color: Colors.grey.shade100,
            // JsonEncoder.withIndent('  '): the JSON, indented by 2 spaces
            child: Text(
              const JsonEncoder.withIndent('  ').convert(_model),
              style: const TextStyle(fontFamily: 'RobotoMono', fontSize: 12),
            ),
          ),
          // a block that only exists after a send; ...[ ] inserts SEVERAL widgets
          if (_sent != null) ...[
            const SizedBox(height: 8),
            Text('Last send', style: titleStyle),
            Container(
              padding: const EdgeInsets.all(8),
              color: Colors.green.shade50,
              child: Text(_sent!, style: const TextStyle(fontFamily: 'RobotoMono', fontSize: 12)),
            ),
          ],
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}

A controlled field displays a value from the state and notifies the widget of any changes ([onChanged]), which updates the state: the state is the single source of truth. This is true for all fields in [Flutter]... except for text boxes, which store their text in a controller.

  • Lines 39–41: The text in [Flutter] itself (the days and months of the calendar, the “OK” and “CANCEL” buttons in its windows) is in English by default. We declare the application’s languages ([supportedLocales]), the selected language ([locale]), and the “delegates” that provide translations for [Flutter], in the [flutter_localizations] package. Example 21 will revisit this;
  • lines 56–66: one state per field. [final _name = TextEditingController()]: for a text field, the state is the control itself; [Set<String>]: a set (without duplicates) of hobbies and languages; [DateTime? _birthDate]: a date, or [null] until one is selected;
  • lines 69–74: [initState] is called once, when the object [State] is created (see Example 13). A controller notifies its listeners ([addListener]) of every change to its text: the screen is redrawn so that the model displayed at the bottom keeps up with the input. [setState(() {})]: nothing needs to be changed, only redrawn;
  • line 87: the date in the format of API [RdvMedecins], “2026-10-05.” [_birthDate?.toIso8601String()]: the [?.] operator calls the method only if [_birthDate] is not [null] (otherwise, the result is [null]);
  • lines 90–100: all values, combined into a [Map] (which would be sent to a server). [int.tryParse(_age.text)]: the age, or [null] if the field is not a number;
  • lines 105–113: the date of birth is selected from a calendar window. [showDatePicker] opens the window and returns a [Future]: the selected date, later, when the user has closed the window (or [null] if they closed it without making a selection). The method is [async]: [await] waits for [Future] to finish without blocking the application. This mechanism is used wherever there is a need to wait (for a window, a server);
  • lines 118–126: the state modified by the code: the fields follow. For a text box, we write to its controller. [..clear()..addAll([...])]: the “cascade” of [Dart], multiple method calls on the same object;
  • line 132: [jsonEncode] (from [dart:convert]) creates the JSON from a [Map].

The fields in [build]:

  • lines 146–151: radio buttons. [RadioGroup] contains the selected value ([groupValue]) and the function called when another value is selected ([onChanged]); it contains the buttons [Radio], each with its own value. [...[a, b, c]] inserts multiple widgets at once: for each title, a button, its label, and a space;
  • lines 160–169: two text fields side by side, in a [Row]. [Expanded(flex: 2, ...)]: the name takes up twice as much space as the age. The age field’s keyboard is numeric;
  • Lines 178–186: An uncontrolled field: [TextFormField] can receive an initial value ([initialValue]) instead of a controller, and manage its own text. The text is updated with each keystroke, WITHOUT [setState]: nothing is redrawn. The [Focus] widget notifies when its child gains or loses focus ([onFocusChange]): redrawing only occurs when the field is exited. This is equivalent to the [blur] event of the HTML;
  • lines 190–195: a single checkbox and its label;
  • lines 199–206: multiple choices for ONE set: checkboxes to select ([FilterChip]). Each bullet is selected if the set contains its value; tapping it adds or removes the value. [Wrap] places its children side by side and wraps to the next line when there is no more space;
  • lines 216–222: a drop-down list. [value] specifies which item is selected; [items] lists the items, each with its value and widget. [for (final MapEntry(key: code, value: name) in countries.entries)] iterates through the entries of the [Map] [countries] by “unpacking” each one into two variables, [code] and [name];
  • lines 230–234: spoken languages, also listed with bullets. (In [Flutter], there is no multiple-choice list: bullets or checkboxes serve this purpose);
  • lines 244–249: a slider, from 1 to 5, in four intervals ([divisions]). Its value is a [double];
  • lines 254–259: the date of birth and the button that opens the calendar;
  • lines 278–279: the model, live: its JSON, indented by two spaces, in the monospaced font included with the application;
  • lines 283–289: a block that only appears after a message is sent: [if] followed by [...[ ]] inserts several widgets, or none at all.

You choose the title, a name, hobbies, and a language; then you open the calendar; then you send:

The following table summarizes what each field transmits to its corresponding function, [onChanged]:

FieldValue TransmittedTextField, TextFormFieldString (text); or the controller is readCheckbox, CheckboxListTilebool? (checked, unchecked, or undetermined)Switch, SwitchListTileboolRadio (in a RadioGroup)the value of the selected button (T?)DropdownButton<T>the value of the selected element (T?)FilterChipbool: Is the bullet point selected?SegmentedButton<T>Set<T>: the selected valuesSliderdoubleshowDatePickerFuture<DateTime?>: the selected date, at a later time

docs.title: 3.6. Example 06: A form, an object, a reducer
docs.text:
Example 05 had a state field for each form field. For a real form, we prefer an object that contains all the values—the model—and we describe its changes in a single function, the reducer: [reducer(currentState, action) -> newState]. This is what the hook [useReducer] does for [React]; in [Flutter], there is nothing to import: [Dart] provides everything needed.

// =========================================================================
// lib/ex06_reducer/main.dart - a form, an object, a reducer
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Example 05 had one state field per field of the form. For a real
// form, we prefer ONE object that holds all the values, the
// MODEL (here a Profile object, not modifiable), and we describe its
// changes in a single function, the REDUCER:
//
//     reducer(currentState, action) -> newState
//
// The widget no longer modifies the state: it DESCRIBES what happened, with a
// ProfileAction object (Edit(Field.lastName, 'Dupont'), Leave(Field.lastName)...), and
// the reducer deduces the new state from it. All the logic is in one
// place, in a PURE function (same input, same output, no side
// effect), easy to test.
// Dart lends itself well to this: a "sealed" class lists all the possible
// actions, and a switch on an action is checked by the compiler
// (a forgotten case is an error).
//
// The state also keeps, for each field, whether it has been "touched" (left at
// least once); from it we deduce whether it is "modified" (its value differs from
// the initial value) and whether it is disabled.
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

// the name of each field of the form
enum Field { title, firstName, lastName, age, newsletter, email, country, birthDate, presentation }

// the data of the form: a NON-MODIFIABLE object (all its fields are
// final). To "modify" it, we build a new one (copyWith)
class Profile {
  final String title;
  final String firstName;
  final String lastName;
  final int age;
  final bool newsletter;
  final String email;
  final String country;
  final String birthDate;
  final String presentation;

  const Profile({
    required this.title,
    required this.firstName,
    required this.lastName,
    required this.age,
    required this.newsletter,
    required this.email,
    required this.country,
    required this.birthDate,
    required this.presentation,
  });

  // a copy, in which a few fields are changed (the others are kept);
  // "??": the new value if it is provided, otherwise the old one
  Profile copyWith({
    String? title,
    String? firstName,
    String? lastName,
    int? age,
    bool? newsletter,
    String? email,
    String? country,
    String? birthDate,
    String? presentation,
  }) {
    return Profile(
      title: title ?? this.title,
      firstName: firstName ?? this.firstName,
      lastName: lastName ?? this.lastName,
      age: age ?? this.age,
      newsletter: newsletter ?? this.newsletter,
      email: email ?? this.email,
      country: country ?? this.country,
      birthDate: birthDate ?? this.birthDate,
      presentation: presentation ?? this.presentation,
    );
  }

  // the value of a field, designated by its name
  Object value(Field c) => switch (c) {
    Field.title => title,
    Field.firstName => firstName,
    Field.lastName => lastName,
    Field.age => age,
    Field.newsletter => newsletter,
    Field.email => email,
    Field.country => country,
    Field.birthDate => birthDate,
    Field.presentation => presentation,
  };

  // a copy in which ONE field, designated by its name, has a new value
  Profile withField(Field c, Object v) => switch (c) {
    Field.title => copyWith(title: v as String),
    Field.firstName => copyWith(firstName: v as String),
    Field.lastName => copyWith(lastName: v as String),
    Field.age => copyWith(age: v as int),
    Field.newsletter => copyWith(newsletter: v as bool),
    Field.email => copyWith(email: v as String),
    Field.country => copyWith(country: v as String),
    Field.birthDate => copyWith(birthDate: v as String),
    Field.presentation => copyWith(presentation: v as String),
  };

  Map<String, Object> toJson() => {for (final c in Field.values) c.name: value(c)};
}

const initial = Profile(
  title: 'Mme',
  firstName: 'Marie',
  lastName: 'PELISSIER',
  age: 30,
  newsletter: false,
  email: '',
  country: 'fr',
  birthDate: '',
  presentation: '',
);

// the complete state: the values, and the fields already left
class ProfileState {
  final Profile values;
  final Set<Field> touched;

  const ProfileState(this.values, this.touched);
}

// the possible actions. "sealed": there are no others than those of
// this file, the compiler knows it
sealed class ProfileAction {
  const ProfileAction();
}

class Edit extends ProfileAction {
  final Field field;
  final Object value;
  const Edit(this.field, this.value);
}

class Leave extends ProfileAction {
  final Field field;
  const Leave(this.field);
}

class Uppercase extends ProfileAction {
  const Uppercase();
}

class Reset extends ProfileAction {
  const Reset();
}

// the reducer: it NEVER modifies the state it receives, it returns a new one.
// The switch "destructures" each action: Edit(:final field, ...) reads
// its fields into variables of the same name
ProfileState reducer(ProfileState state, ProfileAction action) => switch (action) {
  Edit(:final field, :final value) => ProfileState(state.values.withField(field, value), state.touched),
  Leave(:final field) => ProfileState(state.values, {...state.touched, field}),
  Uppercase() => ProfileState(
    state.values.copyWith(firstName: state.values.firstName.toUpperCase(), lastName: state.values.lastName.toUpperCase()),
    state.touched,
  ),
  Reset() => const ProfileState(initial, {}),
};

const titles = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];
const trackedFields = [Field.firstName, Field.lastName, Field.age, Field.email];
// the text fields: each one will have its controller
const textFields = [Field.firstName, Field.lastName, Field.email, Field.presentation];

void main() {
  runApp(
    MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      home: const ProfilePage(),
    ),
  );
}

class ProfilePage extends StatefulWidget {
  const ProfilePage({super.key});

  @override
  State<ProfilePage> createState() => _ProfilePageState();
}

class _ProfilePageState extends State<ProfilePage> {
  ProfileState _state = const ProfileState(initial, {});
  // one controller per text field; a "map": Field -> controller
  final _controllers = {for (final c in textFields) c: TextEditingController(text: initial.value(c) as String)};

  @override
  void dispose() {
    for (final c in _controllers.values) {
      c.dispose();
    }
    super.dispose();
  }

  // THE only way to change the state: describing what happened
  void _dispatch(ProfileAction action) {
    setState(() => _state = reducer(_state, action));
    // the reducer may have changed a text (Uppercase, Reset): the
    // input fields must show it
    for (final MapEntry(key: field, value: controller) in _controllers.entries) {
      final value = _state.values.value(field) as String;
      if (controller.text != value) {
        controller.text = value;
      }
    }
  }

  Profile get _v => _state.values;

  // values DEDUCED from the state
  bool _modified(Field c) => _v.value(c) != initial.value(c);
  bool _disabled(Field c) => c == Field.email && !_v.newsletter; // the e-mail requires the newsletter
  bool get _formModified => Field.values.any(_modified);

  // a text field linked to the model: a method that builds it
  Widget _field(Field field, String label, {int lines = 1}) {
    // Focus: we know when the field is LEFT (it loses the focus)
    return Focus(
      onFocusChange: (hasFocus) {
        if (!hasFocus) _dispatch(Leave(field));
      },
      child: TextField(
        controller: _controllers[field],
        enabled: !_disabled(field),
        maxLines: lines,
        decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: label),
        onChanged: (text) => _dispatch(Edit(field, text)),
      ),
    );
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final titleStyle = Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleSmall;
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Example 06 - a reducer')),
      body: ListView(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
        children: [
          RadioGroup<String>(
            groupValue: _v.title,
            onChanged: (t) => _dispatch(Edit(Field.title, t!)),
            child: Row(
              children: [
                for (final t in titles) ...[Radio<String>(value: t), Text(t), const SizedBox(width: 12)],
              ],
            ),
          ),
          Row(
            children: [
              Expanded(child: _field(Field.firstName, 'First name')),
              const SizedBox(width: 12),
              Expanded(child: _field(Field.lastName, 'Last name')),
            ],
          ),
          Row(
            children: [
              Text('Age: ${_v.age}', style: titleStyle),
              Expanded(
                child: Slider(
                  value: _v.age.toDouble(),
                  max: 120,
                  divisions: 120,
                  onChanged: (a) => _dispatch(Edit(Field.age, a.round())),
                  // the slider is released: the field has been "left"
                  onChangeEnd: (_) => _dispatch(const Leave(Field.age)),
                ),
              ),
            ],
          ),
          SwitchListTile(
            contentPadding: EdgeInsets.zero,
            title: const Text('Receive the newsletter'),
            value: _v.newsletter,
            onChanged: (yes) => _dispatch(Edit(Field.newsletter, yes)),
          ),
          _field(Field.email, 'E-mail (if newsletter)'),
          const SizedBox(height: 8),
          DropdownButton<String>(
            value: _v.country,
            items: const [
              DropdownMenuItem(value: 'fr', child: Text('France')),
              DropdownMenuItem(value: 'be', child: Text('Belgium')),
              DropdownMenuItem(value: 'ch', child: Text('Switzerland')),
            ],
            onChanged: (p) => _dispatch(Edit(Field.country, p!)),
          ),
          _field(Field.presentation, 'Presentation', lines: 2),
          const SizedBox(height: 12),
          Wrap(
            spacing: 8,
            children: [
              OutlinedButton(onPressed: () => _dispatch(const Uppercase()), child: const Text('Name in upper case')),
              OutlinedButton(onPressed: () => _dispatch(const Reset()), child: const Text('Reset')),
            ],
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 16),
          Text('The model, live', style: titleStyle),
          Container(
            padding: const EdgeInsets.all(8),
            color: Colors.grey.shade100,
            child: Text(
              const JsonEncoder.withIndent('  ').convert(_v.toJson()),
              style: const TextStyle(fontFamily: 'RobotoMono', fontSize: 12),
            ),
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 16),
          Text('The state of the fields', style: titleStyle),
          // DataTable: a table, with its columns and its rows
          DataTable(
            columnSpacing: 16,
            headingRowHeight: 36,
            dataRowMinHeight: 28,
            dataRowMaxHeight: 32,
            columns: const [
              DataColumn(label: Text('field')),
              DataColumn(label: Text('touched')),
              DataColumn(label: Text('modified')),
              DataColumn(label: Text('disabled')),
            ],
            rows: [
              for (final c in trackedFields)
                DataRow(
                  cells: [
                    DataCell(Text(c.name)),
                    DataCell(Text('${_state.touched.contains(c)}')),
                    DataCell(Text('${_modified(c)}')),
                    DataCell(Text('${_disabled(c)}')),
                  ],
                ),
            ],
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 8),
          Text.rich(
            TextSpan(
              children: [
                const TextSpan(text: 'form modified: '),
                TextSpan(
                  text: '$_formModified',
                  style: const TextStyle(fontWeight: FontWeight.bold),
                ),
              ],
            ),
          ),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}

The model:

  • line 30: the name of each field in the form;
  • lines 34–43: the form data: a non-editable object, all of whose fields are [final];
  • lines 45–54: a constructor with named parameters, all of which are required ([required]);
  • lines 59–79: To “modify” a non-editable object, a copy is created in which some fields are changed: this is the method [copyWith], a variation of [Flutter] (which we encountered with [TextStyle]). Each parameter is optional ([String? title]: a string or [null]); [title ?? this.title]: the new value if provided, otherwise the old one;
  • lines 84–93: the value of a field designated by its name: an expression [switch] on the enumeration;
  • lines 97–106: a copy in which ONE field, designated by its name, has a new value. [v as String]: the received value (of type [Object], which can be anything) is converted to a string; if it were not a string, it would result in a runtime error;
  • line 109: a [Map] “field name -> value,” created by a [for] within a literal [Map]. [c.name]: the name of an enumeration value (“firstName”);
  • lines 112–121: the initial values;
  • lines 125–129: the complete state: the values, and all fields that have already been processed (“touched”).

Actions and the reducer:

  • lines 134–154: the possible actions: a sealed class ([sealed]) and its four subclasses. [sealed] tells the compiler that there are no subclasses other than those in this file. An action describes what happened: [Edit(Field.lastName, 'Dupont')], [Leave(Field.lastName)]...;
  • lines 160–167: the reducer. It is a pure function: same input, same output, no side effects; it never modifies the received state, but returns a new one. The [switch] applies to the action, and each case is a pattern that tests its type: [Edit(:final field, :final value)] verifies that the action is an [Edit], and stores its [field] and [value] fields in variables of the same name. Since the class is sealed, the compiler verifies that all four actions are handled; adding a fifth one without completing the reducer would result in a compilation error;
  • line 162: a new set, composed of elements from the old set ([...state.touched]) and the field being exited.

The screen:

  • line 193: the screen state: ONE field, the object [ProfileState];
  • line 195: a text field control, in a [Map] created by a [for];
  • Lines 206–213: the ONLY method for changing the state: describe what happened. [_dispatch] (the name [React] gives it) calculates the new state using the reducer, in [setState]. Then, since the reducer may have modified some text (Uppercase, Reset), the values are copied to the controllers that do not already have them;
  • lines 221–223: values derived from the state: a field is modified if its value differs from the initial value; email is disabled without the newsletter; the form is modified if any of its fields are modified ([any]). [Field.values]: the list of enumeration values;
  • lines 226–237: a method that creates a text field linked to the model: its controller, its disabled state ([enabled]), and two actions: [Edit] on each keystroke, [Leave] when it loses focus;
  • In [build], each field describes its changes using an action: [_dispatch(Edit(Field.title, t!))], [_dispatch(const Uppercase())]...;
  • lines 320–338: a table ([DataTable]), with its columns and rows: the status of each field being tracked;
  • lines 344–349: a text composed of several sections with different styles: [Text.rich] and its [TextSpan].

We change the name, exit the field, and subscribe to the newsletter; then we capitalize the name:

All the form’s logic is contained in the reducer—a function of just a few lines, without any widgets—which can be tested on its own. The widgets now simply display the status and describe what is happening.

docs.title: 3.7. Example 07: Validating a form manually
docs.text:
A pure function, [validate(account)], returns field errors; it is called each time [build] is executed, so the errors are always up to date. They are not displayed immediately (an empty form covered in red is unpleasant), only for a field that has already been left. Submitting the form displays all errors.

// =========================================================================
// lib/ex07_validation/main.dart - validating a form, by hand
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A PURE function, validate(account), returns the errors of the fields; we
// call it on each build(), so the errors are always up to date.
// We do not show them right away (an empty form covered in red is
// unpleasant): only for a field already left ("touched"). Sending
// marks all the fields as touched, then only acts if the form
// is valid. A TextField displays an error below the field, in red,
// when it is given an error text: InputDecoration(errorText: ...).
//
// Same rules as the RdvMedecins server ("Create an account" form).
// WARNING: this validation is only a CONVENIENCE for the user (an
// immediate answer, without a round trip to the server). It protects
// nothing: anyone can send the server a request built by
// hand (curl...). The server therefore ALWAYS validates everything again (see example 25).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

enum Field { title, firstName, lastName, login, password, confirmation }

// a "record": a small group of named values, without a class to write
typedef Account = ({String title, String firstName, String lastName, String login, String password, String confirmation});

const titles = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];
final loginFormat = RegExp(r'^[a-z0-9._-]{1,30}$');
const passwordMin = 6;

// the rules: a pure function, which only depends on its argument.
// It returns, for each field in error, its message
Map<Field, String> validate(Account c) {
  final errors = <Field, String>{};
  if (!titles.contains(c.title)) errors[Field.title] = 'Choose a title from the list.';
  if (c.firstName.trim().isEmpty) {
    errors[Field.firstName] = 'The first name is required.';
  } else if (c.firstName.length > 20) {
    errors[Field.firstName] = 'The first name must not exceed 20 characters.';
  }
  if (c.lastName.trim().isEmpty) {
    errors[Field.lastName] = 'The last name is required.';
  } else if (c.lastName.length > 20) {
    errors[Field.lastName] = 'The last name must not exceed 20 characters.';
  }
  if (c.login.isEmpty) {
    errors[Field.login] = 'The login is required.';
  } else if (!loginFormat.hasMatch(c.login)) {
    errors[Field.login] = 'Unaccented lower-case letters, digits, dot, hyphen, underscore.';
  }
  if (c.password.isEmpty) {
    errors[Field.password] = 'The password is required.';
  } else if (c.password.length < passwordMin) {
    errors[Field.password] = 'At least $passwordMin characters.';
  }
  // a rule that compares TWO fields
  if (c.confirmation != c.password) {
    errors[Field.confirmation] = 'The confirmation does not match the password.';
  }
  return errors;
}

void main() {
  runApp(
    MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      home: const AccountPage(),
    ),
  );
}

class AccountPage extends StatefulWidget {
  const AccountPage({super.key});

  @override
  State<AccountPage> createState() => _AccountPageState();
}

class _AccountPageState extends State<AccountPage> {
  String _title = 'Mr';
  // one controller per text field
  final _texts = {
    for (final c in [Field.firstName, Field.lastName, Field.login, Field.password, Field.confirmation])
      c: TextEditingController(),
  };
  final Set<Field> _touched = {};
  bool _submitAttempted = false;
  bool _success = false;

  @override
  void dispose() {
    for (final c in _texts.values) {
      c.dispose();
    }
    super.dispose();
  }

  // the account, as typed: a record built on demand
  Account get _account => (
    title: _title,
    firstName: _texts[Field.firstName]!.text,
    lastName: _texts[Field.lastName]!.text,
    login: _texts[Field.login]!.text,
    password: _texts[Field.password]!.text,
    confirmation: _texts[Field.confirmation]!.text,
  );

  void _send() {
    setState(() {
      _submitAttempted = true;
      _touched.addAll(Field.values); // all the errors appear
      // here, the account would be sent to the server (see example 25)
      _success = validate(_account).isEmpty;
    });
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    // the errors: recomputed on each build(), never stored in the state
    final errors = validate(_account);

    // the error to DISPLAY for a field: only if it has been touched
    String? error(Field c) => _touched.contains(c) ? errors[c] : null;

    // a text field: label, error, and a green check mark if it is touched and valid
    Widget field(Field c, String label, {bool secret = false}) {
      final valid = _touched.contains(c) && !errors.containsKey(c);
      return Focus(
        onFocusChange: (hasFocus) {
          if (!hasFocus) setState(() => _touched.add(c));
        },
        child: TextField(
          controller: _texts[c],
          obscureText: secret, // the characters are hidden
          decoration: InputDecoration(
            labelText: label,
            errorText: error(c),
            // the error may span two lines
            errorMaxLines: 2,
            suffixIcon: valid ? const Icon(Icons.check_circle, color: Colors.green) : null,
          ),
          onChanged: (_) => setState(() => _success = false),
        ),
      );
    }

    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Example 07 - the validation')),
      body: ListView(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
        children: [
          DropdownButton<String>(
            value: _title,
            items: [for (final t in titles) DropdownMenuItem(value: t, child: Text(t))],
            onChanged: (t) => setState(() => _title = t!),
          ),
          field(Field.firstName, 'First name'),
          field(Field.lastName, 'Last name'),
          field(Field.login, 'Login'),
          field(Field.password, 'Password', secret: true),
          field(Field.confirmation, 'Confirmation', secret: true),
          const SizedBox(height: 16),
          FilledButton(onPressed: _send, child: const Text('Create the account')),
          const SizedBox(height: 12),
          if (_submitAttempted && errors.isNotEmpty)
            _Message('The form contains ${errors.length} error(s).', color: Colors.red.shade50),
          if (_success)
            _Message('Valid form: it could be sent to the server.', color: Colors.green.shade50),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}

// a small private widget: a message on a colored background
class _Message extends StatelessWidget {
  final String text;
  final Color color;

  const _Message(this.text, {required this.color});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Container(
      padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
      decoration: BoxDecoration(color: color, borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(8)),
      child: Text(text),
    );
  }
}
  • line 24: the account entered is a record: a small group of named values, with no class to write. [typedef] assigns it a name. A record is written as [(title: 'Mr', firstName: 'Marie', ...)] and read as [account.firstName];
  • lines 27–28: a regular expression (the format of a login) and a constant: the same rules as the server [RdvMedecins];
  • lines 32–59: the rules: a pure function that depends only on its argument and returns a [Map] “error field → message.” The last rule compares TWO fields: the confirmation and the password;
  • lines 82–84: one validator per text field;
  • line 86: fields that have already been exited;
  • lines 99–105: the account, as entered: a record generated on demand based on the validators. [_texts[Field.firstName]!]: Accessing a [Map] returns a value or [null] (the key may be missing); the [!] confirms that it is present;
  • lines 108–113: the submission marks all fields as touched (errors appear), then takes action only if the form is valid;
  • line 120: in [build], errors are recalculated each time; they are never stored in the state;
  • line 123: a local function: the error to display for a field, only if it has been touched;
  • Lines 126–142: a local function that creates a field. [InputDecoration] knows how to display an error: [errorText]. When it is not [null], the field is outlined in red and the message is displayed below it (on no more than two lines: [errorMaxLines]). [suffixIcon]: an icon to the right of the field—in this case, a green checkmark for a filled-in and valid field. [obscureText] masks the characters of a password;
  • lines 165–168: end-of-form messages;
  • lines 176–187: a small private widget, to avoid repeating the same colored box twice.

Fill in a few fields, then submit; then correct everything, and resubmit:

ATTENTION: This validation is merely a convenience for the user—an immediate response without back-and-forth communication with the server. It doesn’t protect anything: anyone can send a manually crafted request to the server ([curl]…), and the code of a mobile app can be modified. The server therefore always revalidates everything (see Example 25).

docs.title: 3.8. Example 08: Flutter Forms, Form, and FormField
docs.text:
The form from Example 07, written using the tools provided by [Flutter] itself. Whereas [React] requires a library ([React Hook Form]), [Flutter] has its own form widgets:

// =========================================================================
// lib/ex08_form/main.dart - Flutter's forms: Form and FormField
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The form of example 07, written with the form tools that
// Flutter provides itself:
//   - Form: a widget that GROUPS form fields (FormField);
//     it is reached through a "global key", GlobalKey<FormState>;
//   - TextFormField, DropdownButtonFormField...: fields that know how to
//     validate themselves. Their validator parameter is a function:
//         (value) -> null if the value is fine, otherwise the error message;
//   - autovalidateMode: WHEN to validate (here, as soon as the user has
//     modified the field, then on each keystroke);
//   - form.validate(): validates ALL the fields, displays their
//     errors, and returns true if everything is fine;
//   - form.save(): calls the onSaved of each field, which stores its
//     value wherever we want.
// The fields are NOT controlled: each one keeps its value, the Form only
// reads it at validation and at saving time.
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

const titles = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];

void main() {
  runApp(
    MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      home: const AccountPage(),
    ),
  );
}

class AccountPage extends StatefulWidget {
  const AccountPage({super.key});

  @override
  State<AccountPage> createState() => _AccountPageState();
}

class _AccountPageState extends State<AccountPage> {
  // the key that gives access to the state of the form (validate, save, reset)
  final _formKey = GlobalKey<FormState>();
  // the key of ONE field: to validate the confirmation again when the password changes
  final _confirmationKey = GlobalKey<FormFieldState<String>>();
  // the password is read in the rule of the confirmation: a controller
  final _password = TextEditingController();
  // the values stored by the onSaved callbacks
  final Map<String, String> _account = {};
  // null: no send yet; '': send refused; otherwise, the JSON sent
  String? _sent;

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _password.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  void _create() {
    final form = _formKey.currentState!;
    if (!form.validate()) {
      setState(() => _sent = '');
      return;
    }
    form.save(); // each onSaved stores its value in _account
    setState(() => _sent = jsonEncode(_account));
  }

  // rule FACTORIES: each one returns a validation function
  FormFieldValidator<String> _required(String message) =>
      (v) => (v == null || v.trim().isEmpty) ? message : null;

  FormFieldValidator<String> _maximum(int max, FormFieldValidator<String> other) =>
      (v) => other(v) ?? (v!.length > max ? 'At most $max characters.' : null);

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Example 08 - Form and FormField')),
      body: Form(
        key: _formKey,
        child: ListView(
          padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
          children: [
            // initialValue: the initial value; the field then manages its own
            DropdownButtonFormField<String>(
              initialValue: 'Mr',
              decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'Title'),
              items: [for (final t in titles) DropdownMenuItem(value: t, child: Text(t))],
              onChanged: (_) {},
              onSaved: (t) => _account['title'] = t!,
            ),
            TextFormField(
              decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'First name'),
              autovalidateMode: AutovalidateMode.onUserInteraction,
              validator: _maximum(20, _required('The first name is required.')),
              onSaved: (v) => _account['firstName'] = v!.trim(),
            ),
            TextFormField(
              decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'Last name'),
              autovalidateMode: AutovalidateMode.onUserInteraction,
              validator: _maximum(20, _required('The last name is required.')),
              onSaved: (v) => _account['lastName'] = v!.trim(),
            ),
            TextFormField(
              decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'Login', errorMaxLines: 2),
              autovalidateMode: AutovalidateMode.onUserInteraction,
              // a rule written directly: an anonymous function
              validator: (v) {
                if (v == null || v.isEmpty) return 'The login is required.';
                if (!RegExp(r'^[a-z0-9._-]{1,30}$').hasMatch(v)) {
                  return 'Unaccented lower-case letters, digits, dot, hyphen, underscore.';
                }
                return null;
              },
              onSaved: (v) => _account['login'] = v!,
            ),
            TextFormField(
              controller: _password,
              obscureText: true,
              decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'Password'),
              autovalidateMode: AutovalidateMode.onUserInteraction,
              validator: (v) {
                if (v == null || v.isEmpty) return 'The password is required.';
                return v.length < 6 ? 'At least 6 characters.' : null;
              },
              // the password changes: the confirmation is validated again
              // (if it has already been typed)
              onChanged: (_) {
                final confirmation = _confirmationKey.currentState!;
                if (confirmation.value?.isNotEmpty ?? false) confirmation.validate();
              },
              onSaved: (v) => _account['password'] = v!,
            ),
            TextFormField(
              key: _confirmationKey,
              obscureText: true,
              decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'Confirmation', errorMaxLines: 2),
              autovalidateMode: AutovalidateMode.onUserInteraction,
              // a rule that reads ANOTHER field
              validator: (v) => v == _password.text ? null : 'The confirmation does not match the password.',
            ),
            const SizedBox(height: 16),
            FilledButton(onPressed: _create, child: const Text('Create the account')),
            const SizedBox(height: 12),
            if (_sent != null)
              Container(
                padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
                decoration: BoxDecoration(
                  color: _sent!.isEmpty ? Colors.red.shade50 : Colors.green.shade50,
                  borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(8),
                ),
                child: Text(_sent!.isEmpty ? 'Invalid form.' : 'Valid form: $_sent'),
              ),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • Line 46: A form named [Form] contains form fields. To interact with it from the code (validate, save), we assign it a global key, [GlobalKey]: an object that provides access to the state of a widget in the tree ([_formKey.currentState]);
  • line 48: the key of ONE field, so it can be revalidated on its own;
  • line 50: a controller for the password: the confirmation rule must read it;
  • line 52: the values stored upon submission;
  • lines 62–69: [validate()] validates all form fields, displays any errors, and returns [true] if everything is correct. [save()] then calls the function [onSaved] for each field, which sets its value;
  • Lines 73–77: rule generators. A validation rule ([FormFieldValidator]) is a function that receives the field’s value and returns [null] if it is valid; otherwise, it returns the error message. [_required('...')] creates a rule; [_maximum(20, other)] creates a rule that first applies the rule [other], then its own ([??]: if the first one finds nothing);
  • line 83: the form and its key;
  • lines 89–94: a drop-down list that is also a form field. [initialValue]: its initial value; after that, the field manages its own value;
  • lines 96–100: a [TextFormField] is a [TextField] that is also a form field: it has a rule ([validator]), a save function ([onSaved]), and an automatic validation mode: [AutovalidateMode.onUserInteraction] validates the field as soon as the user modifies it, and then with every keystroke;
  • lines 112–117: a rule written directly, with two tests;
  • lines 132–134: when the password changes, the confirmation is revalidated using the field’s key, if it has already been entered;
  • line 144: a rule that reads ANOTHER field.

Enter some incorrect values and submit; then correct them:

Which of the two methods should you choose? [Form] and [TextFormField] are sufficient for a form whose rules are written in the application. But in this course, the server’s rules take precedence: the case study has no rules in the application and displays the error returned by the server beneath each field (Example 25). This is the method used in Example 07, which covers fields and their errors.

docs.title: 3.9. Example 09: Formatting Values
docs.text: Each row of the table shows a piece of code and what it displays.

docs.title: 3.9.1. Formatting functions
docs.text:
[Flutter] has no built-in formatting mechanism (the “pipes” from [Angular]): in [build], we call standard functions, stored in a file and testable separately:

// =========================================================================
// lib/ex09_formatting/formatting.dart - "home-made" formatting functions
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Flutter has no mechanism of its own for formatting (Angular has its
// "pipes"): in build(), we call ordinary FUNCTIONS, stored
// in a file and testable on their own:
//     timeRange(slot)           -> "8:00 - 8:20"
//     timeRange(slot, Part.start) -> "8:00"
// Dart also allows ADDING methods to an existing type, with an
// "extension": 'marie pelissier'.capitalized -> 'Marie Pelissier'.
// For dates, numbers, amounts, the intl package knows the
// conventions of each language (see main.dart).
// =========================================================================

// a time slot, as described by the RdvMedecins API
class Slot {
  final int startHour;
  final int startMinute;
  final int endHour;
  final int endMinute;

  const Slot(this.startHour, this.startMinute, this.endHour, this.endMinute);
}

enum Part { all, start, end }

// "8:05" rather than "8:5"
String _time(int h, int m) => '$h:${m.toString().padLeft(2, '0')}';

// an OPTIONAL parameter, with its default value: [Part part = Part.all]
String timeRange(Slot c, [Part part = Part.all]) => switch (part) {
  Part.start => _time(c.startHour, c.startMinute),
  Part.end => _time(c.endHour, c.endMinute),
  Part.all => '${_time(c.startHour, c.startMinute)} - ${_time(c.endHour, c.endMinute)}',
};

// an EXTENSION of the String type: new methods for ALL the strings
extension Formatting on String {
  // "marie pelissier" -> "Marie Pelissier"; \p{L}: a letter, accented or not
  String get capitalized => replaceAllMapped(
    RegExp(r'\p{L}+', unicode: true),
    (m) => m[0]![0].toUpperCase() + m[0]!.substring(1).toLowerCase(),
  );

  // "Marie PELISSIER" -> "MP"
  String get initials =>
      split(RegExp(r'\s+')).where((word) => word.isNotEmpty).map((word) => word[0].toUpperCase()).join();
}

// "2026-10-05" (the format of the RdvMedecins API) -> a date
DateTime toDate(String day) => DateTime.parse(day);
  • lines 16–22: a time slot, as described in API [RdvMedecins]: hours and minutes, as numbers;
  • line 28: “8:05” rather than “8:5”: [padLeft(2, '0')] pads with zeros on the left;
  • lines 31–34: a function with an optional positional parameter (in square brackets), along with its default value: [timeRange(c)] or [timeRange(c, Part.start)];
  • lines 38–47: an extension: it adds methods (in this case, getters) to the type [String], to ALL the strings: ['marie pelissier'.capitalized]. This is a special feature of [Dart], which is very useful for formatting. [replaceAllMapped] replaces each word (a sequence of letters, accented or unaccented: [\p{L}+] with [unicode: true]) with the function’s return value;
  • line 51: “2026-10-05” (the format of API) -> a date ([DateTime]).

docs.title: 3.9.2. The screen
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex09_formatting/main.dart - formatting values
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Each row of the table shows a piece of code and what it displays.
// The formatters of the intl package (DateFormat, NumberFormat) are created
// once and for all, outside the widgets: building them costs more than
// using them.
// The names of the days and months of each language are not loaded
// by default: initializeDateFormatting() loads them, BEFORE runApp.
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:intl/date_symbol_data_local.dart';
import 'package:intl/intl.dart';

import 'formatting.dart';

// dates: "ready-made" formats (yMMMd, yMMMMEEEEd, Hms...), or a pattern
final shortDate = DateFormat.yMMMd('en_US');
final fullDate = DateFormat.yMMMMEEEEd('en_US');
final timeOnly = DateFormat.Hms('en_US');
final frenchDay = DateFormat.yMMMMd('fr_FR');
final pattern = DateFormat('MM/dd/yyyy HH:mm', 'en_US');
// numbers and amounts
final euros = NumberFormat.currency(locale: 'en_US', symbol: '€');
final integer = NumberFormat.decimalPattern('en_US');
final percent = NumberFormat.decimalPercentPattern(locale: 'en_US', decimalDigits: 1);

const day = '2026-10-05'; // a date in the format of the RdvMedecins API
const price = 1234.5;
const rate = 0.055;
const name = 'marie pelissier';
const doctor = {'title': 'Mme', 'firstName': 'Marie', 'lastName': 'PELISSIER'};
const languages = ['Dart', 'Flutter', 'Kotlin', 'Swift', 'SQL'];
const slots = [Slot(8, 0, 8, 20), Slot(8, 20, 8, 40), Slot(14, 5, 14, 25)];

// main can be ASYNCHRONOUS: we wait for the languages to be loaded
Future<void> main() async {
  await initializeDateFormatting('fr_FR');
  await initializeDateFormatting('en_US');
  runApp(
    MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      home: const FormattingPage(),
    ),
  );
}

class FormattingPage extends StatefulWidget {
  const FormattingPage({super.key});

  @override
  State<FormattingPage> createState() => _FormattingPageState();
}

class _FormattingPageState extends State<FormattingPage> {
  DateTime _now = DateTime.now();

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    // (displayed code, value): a row of the table, as a "record"
    final rows = <(String, String)>[
      ('shortDate.format(now)', shortDate.format(_now)),
      ('fullDate.format(now)', fullDate.format(_now)),
      ('timeOnly.format(now)', timeOnly.format(_now)),
      ('pattern.format(now)', pattern.format(_now)),
      ('fullDate.format(toDate(day))', fullDate.format(toDate(day))),
      ('frenchDay.format(toDate(day))', frenchDay.format(toDate(day))),
      ('now.toString()', _now.toString()),
      ('euros.format(price)', euros.format(price)),
      ('integer.format(price)', integer.format(price)),
      ('price.toStringAsFixed(1)', price.toStringAsFixed(1)),
      ('percent.format(rate)', percent.format(rate)),
      ('name.toUpperCase()', name.toUpperCase()),
      ('name.capitalized', name.capitalized),
      ("'RDV'.toLowerCase()", 'RDV'.toLowerCase()),
      ("languages.take(3).join(', ')", languages.take(3).join(', ')),
      ('jsonEncode(doctor)', jsonEncode(doctor)),
      // two transformations in a row: the result of the first goes to the second
      ('name.capitalized.initials', name.capitalized.initials),
    ];

    const codeStyle = TextStyle(fontFamily: 'RobotoMono', fontSize: 11, color: Color(0xFFC7254E));
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Example 09 - the formatting')),
      body: ListView(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
        children: [
          // Table: a simple table; the first column takes 55% of the width
          Table(
            columnWidths: const {0: FractionColumnWidth(0.55)},
            border: TableBorder(horizontalInside: BorderSide(color: Colors.grey.shade300)),
            children: [
              const TableRow(
                children: [
                  Padding(
                    padding: EdgeInsets.all(4),
                    child: Text('In the code', style: TextStyle(fontWeight: FontWeight.bold)),
                  ),
                  Padding(
                    padding: EdgeInsets.all(4),
                    child: Text('Displayed', style: TextStyle(fontWeight: FontWeight.bold)),
                  ),
                ],
              ),
              // a record can be "destructured": (code, value)
              for (final (code, value) in rows)
                TableRow(
                  children: [
                    Padding(
                      padding: const EdgeInsets.all(4),
                      child: Text(code, style: codeStyle),
                    ),
                    Padding(padding: const EdgeInsets.all(4), child: Text(value)),
                  ],
                ),
            ],
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 16),
          Text('Iterating over the entries of a Map', style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleSmall),
          for (final MapEntry(:key, :value) in doctor.entries) Text('$key = $value'),
          const SizedBox(height: 16),
          Text('A home-made function: timeRange', style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleSmall),
          for (final c in slots) Text('${timeRange(c)} (start: ${timeRange(c, Part.start)})'),
          const SizedBox(height: 16),
          Align(
            alignment: Alignment.centerLeft,
            child: OutlinedButton(
              onPressed: () => setState(() => _now = DateTime.now()),
              child: const Text('Refresh the time'),
            ),
          ),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • lines 21–25: date formatters from the [intl] package. [DateFormat] contains “predefined” formats, identified by the parts to be displayed: [yMMMd] (year, abbreviated month, day), [yMMMMEEEEd] (plus the full day of the week), [Hms] (hours, minutes, seconds)... You can also specify a pattern: ['MM/dd/yyyy HH:mm']. The second parameter is the language;
  • lines 27–29: number formatters: amounts, integers, percentages;
  • lines 40–42: the names of the days and months for each language are not loaded by default: [initializeDateFormatting] loads them, before [runApp]. [main] can be asynchronous;
  • lines 65–83: the table: a list of positional records [(code, value)], without field names;
  • lines 93–111: [Table] draws a simple table. [columnWidths]: the first column takes up 55% of the width; [border]: lines between rows. [for (final (code, value) in rows)] breaks down each record;
  • line 124: iterate through the entries in a [Map]: [:key] is a shortcut for [key: key];
  • line 127: the custom function.

For dates, numbers, and amounts, [intl] serves the same purpose as the [Intl] API in web browsers: it understands the conventions of each language (separators, month names, order of components). The table uses the US English conventions (€1,234.50, “month day, year”); note that in French, a thin non-breaking space separates the thousands (1 234,50 €), and the order is “day month year” (the [frenchDay] row).

docs.title: 10. Interim Conclusion
docs.text:
We have seen, example after example, everything needed to write the [Flutter] client for [RdvMedecins]:

RequirementsIn Fluttera screena widget tree, described by `build()`data that changesthe state of a StatefulWidget (setState), or a ChangeNotifierformsTextField and its controllers, InputDecoration.errorTextmultiple screens, addresses, and guardsgo_router (GoRouter, GoRoute, ShellRoute, redirect)shared dataprovider (ChangeNotifierProvider, context.watch / read)waitFuture, Stream, async/await, FutureBuilderHTTP requeststhe HTTP package, a client that handles cookies, an access layer to the APItwo languagesJSON dictionaries, intl, flutter_localizationson-device storageshared_preferences

The [React] client relied on a library as needed; the [Flutter] client uses fewer of them: [Dart] provides asynchronous processing and types, and [Flutter] provides forms, animations, windows, lists, and the theme. All that remains is to put it all together.

docs.title: 7.1. Example 21: A Bilingual Application
docs.text:
A bilingual application has three types of text to translate:

  • application text: labels and messages. These are stored in dictionaries, one per language;
  • dates and amounts: the [intl] package (see Example 09), in the current language;
  • text from the [Flutter] package itself: the buttons on its windows, the days and months in its calendar. The [flutter_localizations] package provides these.

docs.title: 7.1.1. The dictionaries
docs.text:
{
  "APP": {
    "TITLE": "Exemple 21 - deux langues",
    "LANGUAGE": "Langue"
  },
  "HOME": {
    "HELLO": "Bonjour {{name}} !",
    "TODAY": "Nous sommes le {{date}}.",
    "PRICE": "Une consultation coûte {{price}}.",
    "APPOINTMENTS_zero": "aucun rendez-vous",
    "APPOINTMENTS_one": "un rendez-vous",
    "APPOINTMENTS_other": "{{count}} rendez-vous",
    "ADD": "Ajouter un rendez-vous",
    "REMOVE": "En retirer un",
    "CALENDAR": "Ouvrir le calendrier"
  },
  "ERRORS": {
    "LOGIN_TAKEN": "Ce login est déjà utilisé par un autre compte.",
    "TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS": "Trop de tentatives infructueuses. Réessayez dans {{minutes}} minute(s)."
  },
  "SERVER": {
    "TITLE": "Traduire une réponse du serveur",
    "EXPLANATION": "Le serveur RdvMedecins ne renvoie que des clés. C'est le client qui les traduit :"
  }
}

Each text has a key ("HOME.HELLO"). The parameters are written as [{{name}}]; a plural text has multiple keys, such as [_zero], [_one], and [_other]. These are the conventions of the [JavaScript] [i18next] library, used by the [React] and [Vue.js] clients of [RdvMedecins]: The case study will use their dictionaries as-is. The English dictionary has the same keys:

{
  "APP": {
    "TITLE": "Example 21 - two languages",
    "LANGUAGE": "Language"
  },
  "HOME": {
    "HELLO": "Hello {{name}}!",
    "TODAY": "Today is {{date}}.",
    "PRICE": "A consultation costs {{price}}.",
    "APPOINTMENTS_zero": "no appointment",
    "APPOINTMENTS_one": "one appointment",
    "APPOINTMENTS_other": "{{count}} appointments",
    "ADD": "Add an appointment",
    "REMOVE": "Remove one",
    "CALENDAR": "Open the calendar"
  },
  "ERRORS": {
    "LOGIN_TAKEN": "This login is already used by another account.",
    "TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS": "Too many failed attempts. Try again in {{minutes}} minute(s)."
  },
  "SERVER": {
    "TITLE": "Translating a server response",
    "EXPLANATION": "The RdvMedecins server only sends keys. The client translates them:"
  }
}

docs.title: 7.1.2. The translations
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex21_i18n/translations.dart - dictionaries, a current language
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Each language has its DICTIONARY, a JSON file shipped with
// the application (assets/i18n/ex21_en.json, ex21_fr.json), where each text
// has a KEY ("HOME.HELLO"):
//   - t('HOME.HELLO', {'name': 'Marie'}): the text of the CURRENT
//     language, whose {{name}} parameters are replaced;
//   - t('HOME.APPOINTMENTS', {'count': n}): a text in the plural; we
//     choose the key APPOINTMENTS_zero, _one or _other according to n and the rules
//     of the language (in French, 0 and 1 are singular; in English,
//     only 1);
//   - changeLanguage('fr'): loads the other dictionary, and notifies the
//     screens (a ChangeNotifier), which translate themselves again.
// These are the conventions of the i18next JavaScript library: the
// dictionaries are those of the Vue.js, Angular and React clients of
// RdvMedecins... and the server, which only returns KEYS
// ("ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN"), uses them too.
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:flutter/services.dart';
import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart';
import 'package:intl/intl.dart';
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';

const languages = ['en', 'fr'];

class Translations extends ChangeNotifier {
  final String _prefix; // the dictionaries: assets/i18n/<prefix>_<language>.json
  final SharedPreferences? _storage;
  String _language = 'en';
  Map<String, Object?> _dictionary = {};

  Translations(this._prefix, [this._storage]);

  String get language => _language;

  // the initial language: the one stored on the device, otherwise the one of the
  // phone (if it is known), otherwise English
  Future<void> start() async {
    final stored = _storage?.getString('$_prefix.language');
    final device = WidgetsBinding.instance.platformDispatcher.locale.languageCode;
    await changeLanguage(stored ?? (languages.contains(device) ? device : 'en'));
  }

  Future<void> changeLanguage(String language) async {
    // rootBundle: the files shipped with the application (assets section of the pubspec)
    final json = await rootBundle.loadString('assets/i18n/${_prefix}_$language.json');
    _dictionary = jsonDecode(json) as Map<String, Object?>;
    _language = language;
    await _storage?.setString('$_prefix.language', language);
    notifyListeners();
  }

  // "HOME.HELLO" -> dictionary['HOME']['HELLO']; null if missing
  String? _lookUp(String key) {
    Object? node = _dictionary;
    for (final part in key.split('.')) {
      node = node is Map<String, Object?> ? node[part] : null;
    }
    return node is String ? node : null;
  }

  String t(String key, [Map<String, Object?> params = const {}]) {
    String? text;
    final count = params['count'];
    if (count is int) {
      // Intl.pluralLogic: the plural form, according to the rules of the language
      text = Intl.pluralLogic(
        count,
        locale: _language,
        zero: _lookUp('${key}_zero'),
        one: _lookUp('${key}_one'),
        other: _lookUp('${key}_other'),
      );
    }
    text ??= _lookUp(key);
    // an unknown key is displayed as is: what is missing is seen right away
    if (text == null) return key;
    // {{name}} -> the value of the name parameter
    return text.replaceAllMapped(RegExp(r'\{\{(\w+)\}\}'), (m) => '${params[m[1]] ?? m[0]}');
  }
}
  • lines 30–34: the translations: a [ChangeNotifier] (the screens will be rebuilt when the language changes), which retains the current language and its dictionary;
  • lines 42–45: the source language: the one stored on the device, otherwise the phone’s language (if known), otherwise English;
  • lines 48–54: change language: load the dictionary, a JSON file included with the application ([rootBundle.loadString] reads a file from the [assets] section of [pubspec.yaml]), decode it ([jsonDecode]), save the selection, and update the screens;
  • lines 58–63: search for a key “HOME.HELLO” in the dictionary: it traverses, section by section, the nested JSON objects. [node is Map<String, Object?> ? ... : null]: a type check, which “promotes” the variable in the branch where it is true;
  • Lines 66–83: the translation. For a plural (an integer parameter [count]), [Intl.pluralLogic] chooses the form according to the language rules: in French, 0 and 1 are singular; in English, only 1. An unknown key is displayed as-is: you can immediately see what’s missing. Finally, each [{{name}}] is replaced by the parameter’s value.

Why not use the official [Flutter] tool? [Flutter] offers a generator ([flutter gen-l10n]) that creates, from [.arb] files, a class with one method per text ([AppLocalizations.of(context).hello('Marie')]): The keys are validated at compile time. This is the best solution for an application where all texts are known in advance. But our server returns keys (“ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN”) that need to be translated at runtime: a dictionary, which is queried by the key, is much better suited for this purpose and allows us to share dictionaries with other clients.

docs.title: 7.1.3. The translated page
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex21_i18n/main.dart - an application in two languages
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
//   - the TEXTS of the application: the dictionaries (translations.dart),
//     provided to all the screens by provider (see example 20);
//   - the dates and amounts: the intl package, in the current language
//     (see example 09);
//   - the texts of Flutter ITSELF (the calendar, its buttons...): the
//     localization "delegates" of the flutter_localizations package, which
//     follow the locale property of MaterialApp.
// Changing the language translates the whole screen again, without restarting.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter_localizations/flutter_localizations.dart';
import 'package:intl/date_symbol_data_local.dart';
import 'package:intl/intl.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';

import 'translations.dart';

// what the RdvMedecins server would return (see the chapter on the black box)
const serverResponses = [
  (statusCode: 409, key: 'ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN', params: <String, String>{}),
  (statusCode: 429, key: 'ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS', params: {'minutes': '15'}),
];

// context.t('KEY'): a shortcut, through an extension of BuildContext
extension Translate on BuildContext {
  String t(String key, [Map<String, Object?> params = const {}]) => watch<Translations>().t(key, params);
}

Future<void> main() async {
  WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();
  await initializeDateFormatting();
  final translations = Translations('ex21', await SharedPreferences.getInstance());
  await translations.start();
  runApp(ChangeNotifierProvider.value(value: translations, child: const Application()));
}

class Application extends StatelessWidget {
  const Application({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      // onGenerateTitle: the title of the application, translated
      onGenerateTitle: (context) => context.t('APP.TITLE'),
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      locale: Locale(context.watch<Translations>().language),
      supportedLocales: [for (final l in languages) Locale(l)],
      localizationsDelegates: GlobalMaterialLocalizations.delegates,
      home: const TranslatedPage(),
    );
  }
}

class TranslatedPage extends StatefulWidget {
  const TranslatedPage({super.key});

  @override
  State<TranslatedPage> createState() => _TranslatedPageState();
}

class _TranslatedPageState extends State<TranslatedPage> {
  int _count = 2;
  final _today = DateTime.now();

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final translations = context.watch<Translations>();
    final language = translations.language;
    // formatters in the CURRENT language
    final date = DateFormat.yMMMMEEEEd(language).format(_today);
    final price = NumberFormat.currency(locale: language, name: 'EUR', symbol: '€').format(1234.5);

    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(
        title: Text(context.t('APP.TITLE')),
        actions: [
          // the languages: "segmented" buttons
          Padding(
            padding: const EdgeInsets.only(right: 8),
            child: SegmentedButton<String>(
              showSelectedIcon: false,
              segments: [for (final l in languages) ButtonSegment(value: l, label: Text(l.toUpperCase()))],
              selected: {language},
              onSelectionChanged: (choice) => translations.changeLanguage(choice.first),
            ),
          ),
        ],
      ),
      body: ListView(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
        children: [
          Card(
            child: Padding(
              padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
              child: Column(
                crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
                children: [
                  Text(context.t('HOME.HELLO', {'name': 'Marie'})),
                  Text(context.t('HOME.TODAY', {'date': date})),
                  Text(context.t('HOME.PRICE', {'price': price})),
                  const SizedBox(height: 8),
                  // count: chooses the plural form, and replaces {{count}}
                  Text(
                    context.t('HOME.APPOINTMENTS', {'count': _count}),
                    style: const TextStyle(fontWeight: FontWeight.bold),
                  ),
                  Wrap(
                    spacing: 8,
                    children: [
                      TextButton(onPressed: () => setState(() => _count++), child: Text(context.t('HOME.ADD'))),
                      TextButton(
                        onPressed: _count == 0 ? null : () => setState(() => _count--),
                        child: Text(context.t('HOME.REMOVE')),
                      ),
                    ],
                  ),
                  // Flutter's calendar: its texts follow the language of MaterialApp
                  OutlinedButton.icon(
                    icon: const Icon(Icons.calendar_month),
                    label: Text(context.t('HOME.CALENDAR')),
                    onPressed: () =>
                        showDatePicker(context: context, firstDate: DateTime(2026), lastDate: DateTime(2027, 12, 31)),
                  ),
                ],
              ),
            ),
          ),
          Card(
            child: Padding(
              padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
              child: Column(
                crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
                children: [
                  Text(context.t('SERVER.TITLE'), style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleSmall),
                  Text(context.t('SERVER.EXPLANATION')),
                  const SizedBox(height: 8),
                  // the server's key IS a key of the dictionary; params provides its parameters
                  for (final r in serverResponses) ...[
                    Text('${r.statusCode} ${r.key}', style: const TextStyle(fontFamily: 'RobotoMono', fontSize: 12)),
                    Text('→ ${context.t(r.key, r.params)}'),
                    const SizedBox(height: 6),
                  ],
                ],
              ),
            ),
          ),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • lines 30–31: an extension of [BuildContext] (see Example 09): [context.t('KEY')] reads the translations provided above, subscribes to updates, and performs the translation;
  • lines 36–38: initialization: the names of the days and months in all languages, followed by the translations;
  • line 39: [ChangeNotifierProvider.value] provides an object ALREADY created (by [main]);
  • line 50: the application title, translated;
  • lines 52–54: the language of [Flutter] itself follows that of the application;
  • lines 76–77: the date and price, formatted in the current language, then passed as parameters to the text strings;
  • lines 86–90: the language selection in the top bar;
  • line 110: [count] selects the plural form and replaces [{{count}}];
  • lines 124–128: the calendar for [Flutter]: its texts follow the language of [MaterialApp];
