  • lines 144–146: what the server [RdvMedecins] would return: a key and its parameters. The key from the server IS a key from the dictionary.

In English (left); in French, after an addition (middle); the calendar, in French (right):

Changing the language re-renders the entire screen without restarting or making any requests to the server. The selected language is stored on the device.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
The document’s PDF is HERE.

The document’s codes are HERE.

This document is a product of Anthropic’s AI Claude. It follows the course “Step-by-Step Introduction to the React Web Framework,” from which it borrows the outline, examples, and case study, while changing the target:

  • In the courses [React], [Vue.js], and [Angular], the application runs in a browser; it is built using HTML, CSS, and [JavaScript];
  • In this course, the application is a mobile app, written using the [Flutter] framework and the [Dart] language, which runs on a [Android] phone. The same code, without any changes, also generates a web application (and a [Windows], [macOS], or [Linux] application).

The server, however, remains the same: it is the JSON [RdvMedecins] server from previous lessons, written using [NestJS]. And the application screens are the ones that readers of the other lessons are already familiar with (login with CAPTCHA, doctor’s schedule, appointment window, patient portal, doctor and client management, account creation, English and French), adapted for a phone screen.

The document follows the same structure as its predecessors: first, numerous short examples, each focusing on a concept from [Flutter], followed by a complete case study—the [Flutter] client for the [RdvMedecins] application—with all files fully commented. The 25 examples have the same numbers as those in the [React] course: Readers familiar with [React], [Vue.js], or [Angular] will find the same examples, written in the style of [Flutter].

A course on this topic already exists: An Example of a Flutter Client/Server / NestJS (2026), which presents a complete client right from the start. This document differs in its approach: we learn [Flutter] step by step, through small examples, before tackling the complete client; and the server is treated as a black box, of which only the API and JSON are of interest to us.

A basic understanding of the [Dart] language is assumed: these fundamentals are covered in the course “Introduction to the Dart Language Through Examples” (2026). However, language features specific to [Flutter] (named parameters, classes, [async] / [await], collections, etc.) are reviewed throughout the examples as they are used.

docs.title: 1.1. The Role of Flutter in a Client/Server Application
docs.text:
The application has two parts, which communicate with each other only through HTTP requests:

  • 1: The [Flutter] application, running on the phone, sends a HTTP request to the server, for example, [GET /api/schedule?doctorId=1&day=2026-10-05];
  • 2: The server responds with data JSON: this doctor’s schedule for that day. It does not generate any pages;
  • 3: Using this data, [Flutter] updates the phone’s screen.

This is exactly the architecture of the clients [React], [Vue.js], and [Angular]: the only difference is what generates the display. Whereas a browser builds a page from HTML and CSS, [Flutter] draws every pixel on the screen itself, using its own graphics engine. It does not use the system’s components (the buttons from [Android] or [iOS]): it mimics them or provides its own. This is what allows it to display the same application, down to the pixel, on a [Android] phone, a [iPhone], in a browser, or on a computer.

[Flutter] is a framework created by [Google] and released in 2018. It is currently the most widely used framework for writing mobile apps for [Android] and [iOS] using a single codebase. It is based on three core concepts:

  • everything is a widget: the screen is described by a tree of widgets, objects that each represent a part of the interface—such as text, a button, a margin, a column, or an entire screen. You create your own widgets by assembling those provided by [Flutter];
  • the interface is a function of state: a widget has a method [build()] that describes what to display based on its data. When the data changes ([setState()]), [Flutter] calls [build()], compares the new tree to the old one, and redraws what has changed. We never write code that modifies the screen: we describe the screen based on its state. Readers of the [React] course will recognize this principle: it is the same as that of components and [useState];
  • a language, [Dart], compiled into machine code for the phone (resulting in fast applications), or into [JavaScript] or [WebAssembly] for the browser. During development, [Dart] enables hot reloading: a code change is applied to the running application in one second, without losing its state.

Like [React], [Flutter] is not an “all-in-one” framework for communicating with a server: the HTTP client, the router, shared state, and translations are provided by packages (libraries) published on the pub.dev website. This course uses the packages recommended in the [Flutter] documentation and maintained, for the most part, by the [Flutter] team itself: [http] (HTTP requests), [go_router] (the router), [provider] (shared state), [shared_preferences] (on-device storage), [intl] (dates and numbers in each language), [flutter_svg] (images SVG).

docs.title: 1.2. Tools Used
docs.text:
The examples were written and tested using the following tools (their installation is described in the appendix):

  • SDK [Flutter] 3.44, which includes SDK [Dart] 3.12;
  • the [Visual Studio Code] editor and its extension [Flutter] (which also installs the [Dart] extension);
  • [Android Studio], only for its emulator manager, and SDK [Android]: an emulator [Android] (a simulated phone on the computer), or a real phone [Android] connected to the computer;
  • the [Chrome] browser, for the web version of the applications;
  • the DBMS [MySQL] (or [MariaDB]), for example, the one for [Laragon] under [Windows] and [Node.js]: these are required by the JSON server, as described in the chapter introducing it;
  • the command-line tool [curl], which displays the raw HTTP responses.

The packages used are those from the [pubspec.yaml] files: [go_router] 16, [provider] 6, [http] 1.5, [shared_preferences] 2.5, [flutter_svg] 2, [intl], and the packages [flutter_localizations] and [flutter_test] included with [Flutter].

docs.title: 1.3. Screenshots
docs.text: The screenshots in this document were generated automatically by [Flutter] tests ([test/captures] project folders): Each test launches an example, interacts with it as a user would (entering text, tapping buttons), and then instructs the [Flutter] engine to render the screen as an image file at the resolution of a [Android] phone (1080 x 2340 pixels). These are therefore actual screens from the app, rendered by the same engine as on the phone; the only elements missing are the phone’s status bar (time, battery) and the on-screen keyboard. The chapter on the first example shows the same app running on a [Android] emulator.

docs.title: 1.4. The Examples
docs.text:
The code in this document is organized into three folders:

en-flutter-etape-par-etape-sept-2026/
├── examples_flutter/          the 25 small Flutter examples (a single project)
├── rdvmedecins-nestjs-json/   the RdvMedecins JSON server (the "black box")
└── rdvmedecins_flutter/       the Flutter client of the case study

The examples make up a single project, [Flutter], with each example located in a folder within [lib/]:

examples_flutter/
├── android/                    the Android project (generated by Flutter)
├── web/                        the web project (generated by Flutter)
├── windows/                    the Windows project (generated by Flutter)
├── assets/                     the files shipped with the application (images, dictionaries)
├── lib/
│   ├── main.dart               the default entry point (it launches example 01)
│   ├── ex01_first_application/
│   │   └── main.dart           the entry point of example 01
│   ├── ex02_state/
│   ├── ...
│   ├── ex25_server_errors/
│   └── common/                 code shared by examples 22 to 25
├── test/                       the tests (and the making of the screenshots)
├── analysis_options.yaml       the rules of the code analyzer
├── pubspec.yaml                the description of the project and of its packages
└── web_dev_config.yaml         the web development server (examples 22 to 25)

The platform-specific folders ([android/], [web/], [windows/]) are not provided in their entirety: these are small projects—[Android] (web) and [Windows]—that [Flutter] can generate, and which depend on the version of [Flutter] installed. You build them once, then download the packages in a console opened to the [examples_flutter] folder (in [VS Code]: Terminal menu / New Terminal):

flutter create --platforms=android,web,windows --org fr.stahe --project-name examples_flutter .
flutter pub get

[flutter create .] (the period indicates the current folder) completes the project without modifying existing files: the provided [android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml] file (see Example 22) is preserved. If you skip this step, [flutter run] fails on a phone with a misleading message: “Build failed due to use of deleted Android v1 embedding” ([Flutter] cannot find the [Android] project and assumes it is very old).

Then run an example by specifying the [main.dart] file with the [-t] option (for “target”):

flutter run -t lib/ex01_first_application/main.dart

[flutter run] asks which device to run the application on if it finds multiple devices (an emulator [Android], [Chrome], [Windows]...). You can specify this using the [-d] option (for “device”):

flutter run -d emulator-5554 -t lib/ex01_first_application/main.dart
flutter run -d chrome -t lib/ex01_first_application/main.dart

While the application is running, the console accepts a few single-letter commands: r (hot reload: code changes are applied, and the state is preserved), R (hot restart: the application restarts from scratch), q (stop). In [VS Code], you can also open the example file [main.dart] and press F5; the device is then selected in the status bar at the bottom right of the window.

Examples 22 through 25 query the JSON and [RdvMedecins] servers: you will need to have them installed and running, as explained in the chapter dedicated to them.

docs.title: 5. Routing
docs.text: An application has multiple screens. [Flutter] manages them using [Navigator]: a stack of screens, where a new screen ([Navigator.push]) is pushed onto the stack and from which it is popped ([Navigator.pop], or the phone’s Back button). This is sufficient for a small mobile app. But as soon as you want URLs (/doctors/2)—that is, screens that can be referenced, opened from a link, reloaded on the web, and protected by guards—you use a router. The [go_router] package, maintained by the [Flutter] team and recommended in its documentation, is the most widely used.

docs.title: 5.1.1. The data
docs.text:
// "hard-coded" data, so as not to depend on a server in this example
typedef Doctor = ({int id, String title, String firstName, String lastName, String specialty});

const doctors = <Doctor>[
  (id: 1, title: 'Mme', firstName: 'Marie', lastName: 'PELISSIER', specialty: 'general practitioner'),
  (id: 2, title: 'Mr', firstName: 'Paul', lastName: 'TATOU', specialty: 'pediatrician'),
  (id: 3, title: 'Melle', firstName: 'Sophie', lastName: 'DUPONT', specialty: 'general practitioner'),
];

"Hard-coded" data, to avoid relying on a server in this example: a list of records.

docs.title: 5.1.2. The routes
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex17_router/routes.dart - the ROUTES of the application
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// An application has several screens ("pages"). The ROUTER associates an
// ADDRESS (a path, as on the web: /doctors/2) with a screen. Flutter
// provides the Navigator (a STACK of screens: we push, we pop); the
// go_router package, maintained by the Flutter team, adds the
// addresses to it: links, parameters, the browser's Back button
// and addresses typed by hand on the web, Android's Back button.
//   '/doctors/:id'   :id is a parameter (/doctors/2 -> id = "2");
//   ShellRoute       a common "shell" (top bar, bottom
//                    navigation bar) around the screens of its routes;
//   redirect         a redirect: the old address leads to the new one;
//   errorBuilder     the screen of an address that matches no route.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';

import 'shell.dart';
import 'pages/home.dart';
// DEFERRED loading: on the web, the code of this page is only downloaded
// on the first visit (flutter build web makes a separate file of it)
import 'pages/about.dart' deferred as about;
import 'pages/deferred_loading.dart';
import 'pages/doctor_detail.dart';
import 'pages/doctor_list.dart';
import 'pages/not_found_page.dart';
import 'pages/search.dart';

final router = GoRouter(
  // the starting address (on a phone: there is no address bar)
  initialLocation: '/',
  routes: [
    ShellRoute(
      // child: the screen of the current child route, placed IN the shell
      builder: (context, state, child) => Shell(child: child),
      routes: [
        GoRoute(path: '/', builder: (context, state) => const Home()),
        GoRoute(
          path: '/doctors',
          builder: (context, state) => const DoctorList(),
          // a NESTED route: /doctors/2
          routes: [
            GoRoute(
              path: ':id',
              // pathParameters: the parameters of the path, always STRINGS
              builder: (context, state) => DoctorDetail(id: state.pathParameters['id']!),
            ),
          ],
        ),
        GoRoute(
          path: '/search',
          // uri.queryParameters: the parameters after the ? (/search?q=pediatrician)
          builder: (context, state) => Search(q: state.uri.queryParameters['q'] ?? ''),
        ),
        GoRoute(
          path: '/about',
          builder: (context, state) =>
              DeferredLoading(load: about.loadLibrary, builder: () => about.About()),
        ),
        // a redirect: the route has no screen, it returns another address
        GoRoute(path: '/physicians', redirect: (context, state) => '/doctors'),
      ],
    ),
  ],
  errorBuilder: (context, state) => NotFoundPage(address: state.uri.toString()),
);

A route associates a path with a screen.

  • Line 23: a deferred import ([deferred]). On the web, this page’s code is compiled into a separate file, which is downloaded only on the first visit to the page ([about.loadLibrary()]). On a phone, all the code is already in the app: [loadLibrary()] terminates immediately;
  • lines 30–32: the router, an object named [GoRouter], is created once, outside of any widget. [initialLocation]: the starting address (on a phone, there is no address bar to display it);
  • lines 34–36: a [ShellRoute] is a common container for several screens: the top bar and the bottom navigation bar. Its [builder] receives [child]—the current route screen—and places it within the shell. This is equivalent to nested routes and the [<Outlet />] of [React Router];
  • line 38: a route—its path—and a function that generates its screen. [state] ([GoRouterState]) describes the current navigation: the address and its parameters;
  • lines 40–47: the list of doctors, and a nested route: [':id'] under ['/doctors'] provides the path [/doctors/:id], where [:id] is a parameter ([/doctors/2]: [id] equals ["2"]). [state.pathParameters] provides the path parameters, which are always strings;
  • lines 52–54: [state.uri] is the full address; [queryParameters] contains the parameters following [?] ([/search?q=pediatrician]);
  • lines 57–59: the page loaded on demand by the [DeferredLoading] widget (discussed later);
  • line 62: a redirect—the route has no screen; its function [redirect] returns another address, to which navigation is redirected;
  • line 66: the screen for an address that does not correspond to any route.

docs.title: 5.1.3. Startup
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex17_router/main.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MaterialApp.router: the application no longer has ONE home screen (home),
// the router decides on the screen, from the address.
// usePathUrlStrategy(): on the web, "clean" addresses (/doctors/2)
// rather than the default form (/#/doctors/2). No effect elsewhere.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter_web_plugins/url_strategy.dart';

import 'routes.dart';

void main() {
  usePathUrlStrategy();
  runApp(
    MaterialApp.router(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      routerConfig: router,
    ),
  );
}
  • line 16: on the web, “clean” addresses ([/doctors/2]) rather than the default form ([/#/doctors/2]). Has no effect on a phone;
  • Lines 17–21: [MaterialApp.router]: the app no longer displays ONE home screen ([home]); the router determines the screen based on the address.

docs.title: 5.1.4. The app's shell
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex17_router/shell.dart - the "shell" of the application
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The top bar, the bottom navigation bar, and, between the two,
// the screen of the current route (child).
//   - GoRouterState.of(context).uri : the current address;
//   - context.go('/doctors')        : going to an address. The stack of
//     screens is REPLACED by the one of this address (a tab);
//   - context.push('/doctors/2')    : PUSHING a screen above the
//     current screen; the Back button (or context.pop()) pops it.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';

// the tabs: (path, label, icon)
const tabs = [
  ('/', 'Home', Icons.home),
  ('/doctors', 'Doctors', Icons.people),
  ('/search?q=general practitioner', 'Search', Icons.search),
  ('/about', 'About', Icons.info),
];

class Shell extends StatelessWidget {
  final Widget child;

  const Shell({super.key, required this.child});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final address = GoRouterState.of(context).uri;
    // the active tab: the one whose path is the start of the current address
    int active = 0;
    for (final (i, (path, _, _)) in tabs.indexed) {
      final start = Uri.parse(path).path;
      if (start != '/' && address.path.startsWith(start)) active = i;
    }

    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Example 17 - the router')),
      body: Column(
        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch,
        children: [
          Container(
            color: Colors.grey.shade100,
            padding: const EdgeInsets.all(8),
            // Uri.decodeFull: %20 becomes a space again
            child: Text(
              'current address: ${Uri.decodeFull(address.toString())}',
              style: const TextStyle(fontFamily: 'RobotoMono', fontSize: 12),
            ),
          ),
          Expanded(
            child: Padding(padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16), child: child),
          ),
        ],
      ),
      // NavigationBar: the bottom tab bar, typical of a mobile
      bottomNavigationBar: NavigationBar(
        selectedIndex: active,
        onDestinationSelected: (i) => context.go(tabs[i].$1),
        destinations: [
          for (final (_, label, icon) in tabs) NavigationDestination(icon: Icon(icon), label: label),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • Lines 17–21: the tabs: records (path, label, icon);
  • line 31: the current address. [GoRouterState.of(context)] is an inherited data read (see Example 14): the shell is reconstructed with each navigation;
  • lines 33–36: the active tab: the one whose path is the beginning of the current address. [for (final (i, (path, _, _)) in tabs.indexed)] parses both the (rank, tab) pair and the tab record, retaining only the path ([_]: “ignored”);
  • lines 48–49: the current address, displayed ([Uri.decodeFull]: [%20] becomes a space again);
  • lines 53–54: the current route screen;
  • lines 59–63: the bottom tab bar ([NavigationBar]), typical of a mobile app. [onDestinationSelected] receives the index of the tapped tab; [context.go(path)] leads to its address. [tabs[i].$1]: the first field of a positional record.

Two ways to navigate, using [go_router]:

  • [context.go('/doctors')]: Go to an address. The screen stack is replaced by the one described by this address. This is what you do to switch tabs;
  • [context.push('/doctors/2')]: Push the screen at this address onto the top of the current screen. The phone’s Back button (or [context.pop()]) pops it off the stack, and you return to where you were. This is how you “enter” a detail view.

// lib/ex17_router/pages/home.dart
// Title: the title of the browser tab (web) or of the application in
// the list of recent applications (Android), as long as the page is displayed
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';

class Home extends StatelessWidget {
  const Home({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Title(
      title: 'Home',
      color: Colors.indigo,
      child: ListView(
        children: [
          const Text(
            'Welcome. Touch the tabs: the screen changes, and so does its address. On the web, '
            "the address is displayed in the browser's bar, the Back and Forward buttons "
            'work, as well as the reload (F5) of any page.',
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 16),
          // links to particular addresses
          Wrap(
            spacing: 8,
            children: [
              OutlinedButton(onPressed: () => context.go('/physicians'), child: const Text('/physicians (redirect)')),
              OutlinedButton(onPressed: () => context.go('/unknown-page'), child: const Text('Broken link')),
            ],
          ),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}

Each page places a [Title] widget: its title is that of the browser tab (on the web) or of the app in the list of recent apps (on [Android]), as long as the page is displayed. Two buttons lead to specific URLs: the redirect [/physicians], and a URL that does not exist.

// lib/ex17_router/pages/doctor_list.dart - links with a parameter
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';

import '../data.dart';

class DoctorList extends StatelessWidget {
  const DoctorList({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Title(
      title: 'Doctors',
      color: Colors.indigo,
      child: ListView(
        children: [
          for (final m in doctors)
            ListTile(
              title: Text('${m.title} ${m.firstName} ${m.lastName}'),
              trailing: const Icon(Icons.chevron_right),
              // push: the doctor's screen is PUSHED; the Back button returns here
              onTap: () => context.push('/doctors/${m.id}'),
            ),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • Line 22: Tapping a doctor pushes its screen onto the stack. 
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex17_router/pages/doctor_detail.dart - a page with a parameter
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The router passes it the :id parameter of the path, a STRING ("2").
// context.pop() pops the screen (like the Back button); context.go()
// leads to another address. If we go from /doctors/1 to /doctors/2,
// Flutter reuses the same screen, simply rebuilt with another id.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';

import '../data.dart';

class DoctorDetail extends StatelessWidget {
  final String id;

  const DoctorDetail({super.key, required this.id});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    // int.tryParse: null if id is not a number; firstWhere... orElse: not found
    final number = int.tryParse(id);
    final found = doctors.where((m) => m.id == number);
    if (found.isEmpty) {
      return Text('Doctor no. $id does not exist.', style: const TextStyle(color: Colors.red));
    }
    final doctor = found.first;
    final next = doctor.id % doctors.length + 1;
    return Title(
      title: '${doctor.firstName} ${doctor.lastName}',
      color: Colors.indigo,
      child: Column(
        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
        children: [
          Text('${doctor.title} ${doctor.firstName} ${doctor.lastName}', style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleLarge),
          Text('Specialty: ${doctor.specialty}'),
          const SizedBox(height: 16),
          Wrap(
            spacing: 8,
            children: [
              OutlinedButton(
                // canPop: is there a screen below? (not if we arrived
                // directly at this address, on the web)
                onPressed: () => context.canPop() ? context.pop() : context.go('/doctors'),
                child: const Text('Back'),
              ),
              FilledButton(
                // pushReplacement: replaces the current screen (no pushing)
                onPressed: () => context.pushReplacement('/doctors/$next'),
                child: const Text('Next doctor'),
              ),
            ],
          ),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • line 16: the path parameter [:id], which the router passes to the constructor;
  • lines 23–26: [int.tryParse]: the numeric ID, or [null]; if a doctor cannot be found, a message is displayed;
  • line 45: Back: the screen is popped off the stack if there is one below it ([canPop]); otherwise (if you arrived directly at this address via the web), you go to the list;
  • line 50: the next doctor replaces the current screen (no stacking: the Back button returns to the list, not to the previous doctor). 
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex17_router/pages/search.dart - a page driven by the address
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// /search?q=pediatrician: the page is entirely described by its address.
// On the web, it can be bookmarked, reloaded, we can go
// back. Searching means GOING to the address /search?q=<input>:
// the page displays what the address says, and nothing else.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';

import '../data.dart';

class Search extends StatelessWidget {
  final String q;

  const Search({super.key, required this.q});

  void _search(BuildContext context, String input) {
    // Uri: builds the address, encoding what is needed (space -> %20)
    context.go(Uri(path: '/search', queryParameters: {'q': input.trim()}).toString());
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final results = doctors
        .where((m) => '${m.firstName} ${m.lastName} ${m.specialty}'.toLowerCase().contains(q.toLowerCase()))
        .toList();
    return Title(
      title: 'Search',
      color: Colors.indigo,
      child: ListView(
        children: [
          // a NON-controlled field, which starts with the value of the address;
          // key: ValueKey(q): if the address changes (Back button), Flutter
          // recreates the field, which then takes the new value
          TextFormField(
            key: ValueKey(q),
            initialValue: q,
            decoration: const InputDecoration(hintText: 'name or specialty', suffixIcon: Icon(Icons.search)),
            textInputAction: TextInputAction.search,
            onFieldSubmitted: (input) => _search(context, input),
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 8),
          for (final m in results) ListTile(title: Text('${m.firstName} ${m.lastName} (${m.specialty})')),
          if (results.isEmpty)
            const ListTile(
              title: Text('No result.', style: TextStyle(color: Colors.grey)),
            ),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • Lines 20–22: Searching means GOING to the address [/search?q=<input>]. [Uri] generates the address by encoding the necessary information (a space becomes [%20]). The page is fully described by its address: on the web, you can bookmark it, reload it, or go back;
  • lines 38–43: an unvalidated field that starts with the value of the URL. [key: ValueKey(q)]: if the URL changes (browser’s Back button), the key changes; [Flutter] recreates the field, which takes on the new value. [textInputAction: TextInputAction.search]: The Enter key on the phone’s keyboard acts as a magnifying glass. 
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex17_router/pages/deferred_loading.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A screen whose code is loaded on demand ("deferred" import):
// load() downloads the code (a Future), builder() builds the screen
// once the code has arrived. Meanwhile: a loading indicator.
// FutureBuilder rebuilds its content when the Future completes
// (see example 19).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

class DeferredLoading extends StatefulWidget {
  final Future<void> Function() load;
  final Widget Function() builder;

  const DeferredLoading({super.key, required this.load, required this.builder});

  @override
  State<DeferredLoading> createState() => _DeferredLoadingState();
}

class _DeferredLoadingState extends State<DeferredLoading> {
  // the Future is created ONCE (and not on each build)
  late final Future<void> _loading = widget.load();

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return FutureBuilder(
      future: _loading,
      builder: (context, snapshot) => snapshot.connectionState == ConnectionState.done
          ? widget.builder()
          : const Center(child: CircularProgressIndicator()),
    );
  }
}
  • line 25: the code is loaded, initiated ONCE (a [late] field initialized on its first read): if it were initiated in [build], each reconstruction would trigger it again;
  • Lines 29–33: [FutureBuilder] rebuilds its content when [Future] terminates: in the meantime, a loading indicator; then, the screen (see Example 19).

// =========================================================================
// lib/ex18_guards/session.dart - a SIMULATED session (without a server)
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The logged-in user must be known to the SCREENS (the top bar,
// the schedule) and to the GUARDS of the router (functions, which are not
// widgets). It is stored in a single object, a ChangeNotifier:
//   - a private field, the state;
//   - methods to read and modify it;
//   - notifyListeners(): notifies its subscribers (the router, the screens)
//     when it changes.
// (Example 23 will do the same thing with a real server.)
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';

enum Role { admin, doctor, user }

typedef User = ({String login, Role role});

// three "hard-coded" accounts (password = login)
const _accounts = {'admin': Role.admin, 'pelissier': Role.doctor, 'martin': Role.user};

class Session extends ChangeNotifier {
  User? _user; // the state: null, nobody is logged in

  User? get user => _user;

  bool logIn(String login, String password) {
    final role = _accounts[login];
    if (role == null || password != login) {
      return false;
    }
    _user = (login: login, role: role);
    notifyListeners();
    return true;
  }

  void logOut() {
    _user = null;
    notifyListeners();
  }
}

// the single session of the application
final session = Session();

The logged-in user must be recognized by the screens (the top bar, the schedule) and the router’s controls—features that are not widgets. It is stored in a single object, a [ChangeNotifier] (see Example 14):

  • line 24: the status: a user, or [null];
  • lines 28–35: the connection, simulated: three “hard-coded” accounts (password = login). It notifies its subscribers ([notifyListeners()]);
  • line 45: the application’s single session, a global variable. (Example 23 will do the same thing with a real server.)

docs.title: 5.2.2. Guards and Protected Paths
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex18_guards/routes.dart - routes PROTECTED by guards
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// redirect: a function that go_router calls BEFORE each navigation
// (the one of the GoRouter: for all the routes; the one of a GoRoute:
// for it alone). It receives the state of the navigation (state.uri:
// the requested address) and returns:
//   - null: the navigation continues;
//   - an address: the navigation is replaced by a navigation to
//     this address.
// refreshListenable: an object to LISTEN to; when it notifies a
// change (the session: login, logout), the router re-evaluates
// its guards for the current screen.
//
// It is the client-side equivalent of the NestJS guards (JwtAuthGuard,
// RolesGuard) - with a FUNDAMENTAL difference: a client guard is
// only a convenience. The application is in the hands of the user, who
// can modify it at will. The real protection of the data remains that
// of the SERVER (see the chapter on the black box).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';

import 'shell.dart';
import 'pages/home.dart';
import 'pages/administration.dart' deferred as administration;
import 'pages/schedule.dart';
import 'pages/login.dart';
import '../ex17_router/pages/deferred_loading.dart';
import 'session.dart';

// the "login required" guard: not logged in -> to the login page,
// remembering where the user wanted to go
String? requireLogin(GoRouterState state) {
  if (session.user == null) {
    return Uri(path: '/login', queryParameters: {'redirect': state.uri.toString()}).toString();
  }
  return null;
}

// the "role required" guard: a function that BUILDS a guard
String? Function(GoRouterState) requireRole(Set<Role> roles) {
  return (state) {
    final u = session.user;
    if (u == null || !roles.contains(u.role)) {
      // logged in, but not with the right role: back to home, with a reason
      return Uri(path: '/', queryParameters: {'denied': state.uri.path}).toString();
    }
    return null;
  };
}

final router = GoRouter(
  refreshListenable: session,
  routes: [
    ShellRoute(
      builder: (context, state, child) => Shell(child: child),
      routes: [
        GoRoute(
          path: '/',
          builder: (context, state) => Home(denied: state.uri.queryParameters['denied']),
        ),
        GoRoute(
          path: '/login',
          builder: (context, state) => Login(redirectTo: state.uri.queryParameters['redirect']),
        ),
        GoRoute(
          path: '/schedule',
          redirect: (context, state) => requireLogin(state),
          builder: (context, state) => const Schedule(),
        ),
        GoRoute(
          path: '/administration',
          // the guards, in order: the first one that returns an address wins
          redirect: (context, state) => requireLogin(state) ?? requireRole({Role.admin})(state),
          // the code of the page is only loaded once the guards are passed
          builder: (context, state) =>
              DeferredLoading(load: administration.loadLibrary, builder: () => administration.Administration()),
        ),
      ],
    ),
  ],
  // any other address (no route matches): back to home
  onException: (context, state, router) => router.go('/'),
);

With [go_router], a guard is a redirect function, called before each navigation (the one for [GoRouter]: for all routes; the one for [GoRoute]: for that route alone). It receives the navigation state and returns:

  • [null]: the navigation continues;
  • an address: the navigation is replaced by a navigation to that address.

The code:

  • lines 34–38: the “connection required” guard: not connected? Redirects to the login page, while retaining the intended destination (parameter [redirect]);
  • lines 42–47: the “role required” guard is generated by a function that receives the permitted roles and returns the guard. Logged in, but without the correct role: redirect to the home page, with a reason (parameter [denied]);
  • line 54: the router monitors the session: when it detects a change (login, logout), it reevaluates the guards for the current screen. If you log out from the schedule, you are immediately redirected to the login page;
  • line 69: the schedule requires the user to be logged in;
  • line 75: the administration page requires the user to be logged in AND to have the role (ADMIN): the checks are chained with [??]; the first one that returns an address takes precedence;
  • Lines 77–78: The code for the administration page is loaded only after the guards have been passed;
  • line 84: any other address redirects to the home page.

This is the client-side equivalent of the server checks [NestJS] ([JwtAuthGuard], [RolesGuard]), with one FUNDAMENTAL difference: a client-side guard is merely a convenience (to avoid displaying an unnecessary screen). The application is in the user’s hands, who can modify it as they wish; true data protection remains on the server, which re-verifies everything with every request (see the chapter on the black box).

// =========================================================================
// lib/ex18_guards/shell.dart - the links, and the logged-in user
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// ListenableBuilder: rebuilds its content each time the listened
// object (the session) notifies a change. The top bar therefore
// follows the logged-in user.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';

import 'session.dart';

class Shell extends StatelessWidget {
  final Widget child;

  const Shell({super.key, required this.child});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final path = GoRouterState.of(context).uri.path;

    // a link: in bold if it designates the displayed page
    Widget link(String target, String label) => TextButton(
      onPressed: () => context.go(target),
      child: Text(label, style: TextStyle(fontWeight: path == target ? FontWeight.bold : FontWeight.normal)),
    );

    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(
        title: const Text('Example 18 - the guards'),
        actions: [
          ListenableBuilder(
            listenable: session,
            builder: (context, _) {
              final u = session.user;
              if (u == null) {
                return TextButton(onPressed: () => context.go('/login'), child: const Text('log in'));
              }
              return Row(
                children: [
                  Chip(label: Text('${u.login} ${u.role.name.toUpperCase()}')),
                  IconButton(
                    tooltip: 'log out',
                    icon: const Icon(Icons.logout),
                    onPressed: () {
                      session.logOut();
                      context.go('/');
                    },
                  ),
                ],
              );
            },
          ),
        ],
      ),
      body: Column(
        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
        children: [
          Wrap(
            children: [
              link('/', 'Home'),
              link('/schedule', 'Schedule (logged in)'),
              link('/administration', 'Administration (ADMIN)'),
            ],
          ),
          const Divider(),
          Expanded(
            child: Padding(padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16), child: child),
          ),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • lines 24–26: a local function that creates a link: in bold if it refers to the currently displayed page;
  • lines 33–37: [ListenableBuilder] rebuilds its content every time the monitored object (the session) signals a change: the top bar follows the logged-in user;
  • lines 46–48: logout, then the welcome page. 
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex18_guards/pages/login.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// After logging in, the user is sent back to the page they wanted to
// open (?redirect=... parameter set by the guard), or to home.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';

import '../session.dart';

class Login extends StatefulWidget {
  final String? redirectTo;

  const Login({super.key, this.redirectTo});

  @override
  State<Login> createState() => _LoginState();
}

class _LoginState extends State<Login> {
  final _login = TextEditingController();
  final _password = TextEditingController();
  bool _error = false;

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _login.dispose();
    _password.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  void _submit() {
    if (!session.logIn(_login.text.trim(), _password.text)) {
      setState(() => _error = true);
      return;
    }
    // only an INTERNAL path is accepted: it starts with /, but not with //
    // (//site.com/... designates ANOTHER site) - no redirect to another site
    final r = widget.redirectTo;
    final internal = r != null && r.startsWith('/') && !r.startsWith('//');
    context.go(internal ? r : '/');
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return ListView(
      children: [
        if (widget.redirectTo != null)
          Card(
            color: Colors.amber.shade50,
            child: Padding(
              padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
              child: Text('Log in to open ${widget.redirectTo}.'),
            ),
          ),
        TextField(
          controller: _login,
          decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'login'),
        ),
        TextField(
          controller: _password,
          obscureText: true,
          decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'password'),
          onSubmitted: (_) => _submit(),
        ),
        const SizedBox(height: 16),
        Align(
          alignment: Alignment.centerLeft,
          child: FilledButton(onPressed: _submit, child: const Text('Log in')),
        ),
        if (_error)
          const Padding(
            padding: EdgeInsets.only(top: 8),
            child: Text('Incorrect login or password.', style: TextStyle(color: Colors.red)),
          ),
      ],
    );
  }
}
  • lines 41–43: After login, the user is redirected to the page they wanted to open (parameter [redirect] set by the guard), or to the home page. Only an internal path is accepted: it begins with [/], but not with [//] ([//site.com/...] refers to ANOTHER site). On the web, a login URL generated by a third party ([/login?redirect=//pirate-site.com]) will therefore never lead anywhere else.

The other pages are very simple:

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

class Home extends StatelessWidget {
  // ?denied=...: set by the requireRole guard when the role does not fit
  final String? denied;

  const Home({super.key, this.denied});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return ListView(
      children: [
        if (denied != null)
          Card(
            color: Colors.red.shade50,
            child: Padding(padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12), child: Text('Your role does not allow opening $denied.')),
          ),
        const Text(
          'Public page. Try the two other links, logged in or not '
          '(admin, pelissier, martin - password = login).',
        ),
      ],
    );
  }
}

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

import '../session.dart';

class Schedule extends StatelessWidget {
  const Schedule({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Text.rich(
      TextSpan(
        children: [
          const TextSpan(text: 'The schedule of '),
          TextSpan(
            text: session.user?.login,
            style: const TextStyle(fontWeight: FontWeight.bold),
          ),
          const TextSpan(text: ': this page requires being logged in.'),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}

docs.title: 2.3. Android Studio and Android command-line tools
docs.text:
The target device for this course is a [Android] phone. To compile the application and install it on this phone, [Flutter] requires the [Android] SDK, which are installed along with [Android Studio], Google's development environment. [Android Studio] is not used for writing code—the editor remains [VSCode]—it is used here solely to install and update the [Android] SDK.

  1. [Android Studio]: Download it for free from [https://developer.android.com/studio] and then install it. When you launch it for the first time, the wizard will offer a standard installation: accept it, and it will download the [Android] SDK.

  1. Open [SDK Manager] from [Android Studio] (the [Tools / SDK Manager] menu when a project is open, or [More Actions / SDK Manager] from the home screen): This is the file that installs and updates the components of the [Android] SDK.
  1. [SDK Platforms] tab: Verify that a recent [Android] platform is installed (the [Flutter] documentation specifies version 36 at the time of writing).

  1. [SDK Tools] tab: Check [Android SDK Command-line Tools (latest)], [Android SDK Build-Tools], and [Android SDK Platform-Tools] (as well as [Android Emulator] if you want to test on an emulator), then click [Apply]. The documentation for [Flutter] also recommends [CMake] and [NDK (Side by side)]. It is the [Android SDK Command-line Tools] packages that are missing when [flutter doctor] displays “cmdline-tools component is missing.”
  2. Accept the licenses for the [Android] SDK by entering the following command in a terminal within the Flutter project, then answering “[y]” to each question until you see the message “All SDK package licenses accepted.”: 
flutter doctor --android-licenses

[Note]: With version 23.0 of [Android SDK Command-line Tools], the command above may complete immediately, without prompting for anything, displaying “The --licenses option is no longer needed.” This is a known issue in [Flutter] (issues 191558 and 191487 on github.com/flutter/flutter). Workaround: In [SDK Manager], [SDK Tools] tab, check [Show Package Details], replace version 23.0 of [Android SDK Command-line Tools] with version 22.0, click on [Apply], and then rerun the command.

If you don’t have a phone, you can test the app on a [Android] emulator: a virtual phone that runs in a window on your computer. [Android Studio] installs the [Android Emulator] program (if it was checked in the [SDK Manager], see above) but does not provide a ready-to-use virtual device: you must create one.

[Prerequisite]: Virtualization must be enabled in the computer’s [BIOS], and under [Windows], the [Windows Hypervisor Platform] feature must be checked ([Control Panel / Programs / Turn Windows features on or off]), which requires a restart. Otherwise, the emulator will not start or will remain very slow.

  1. Start the emulator using the [Play] button on the [Device Manager]:

  1. Wait until the [Android] home screen appears in the emulator window: the first startup may take several minutes. Then verify that [Flutter] recognizes the emulator, which should appear in the list (for example, [emulator-5554], platform [android-x64]): 
flutter devices

Try the following in order: (1) wait for the welcome screen to appear, then rerun the command; (2) restart [adb] using the following three commands (in [Windows], within [PowerShell]), with the last one displaying “device” rather than “offline”; (3) In the device’s [Device Manager] menu ([⋮]), select [Cold Boot Now], or even [Wipe Data] as a last resort.

& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Android\Sdk\platform-tools\adb.exe" kill-server

Preparing the Android phone

To run the application on a real [Android] phone, the phone must be set to allow control from the computer:

  1. Enable developer options: open [Settings / About phone], then tap [Build number] several times (usually 7) until the phone indicates that you are a developer. The exact labels vary by manufacturer.
  2. Enable [USB debugging] in the [Developer options] menu (added in the previous step).
  3. Connect the phone to the computer using a USB cable that transfers data (not just charges the phone), and accept the USB debugging authorization request on the phone. On Windows, if the phone is not recognized, install the manufacturer’s driver USB (“OEM USB drivers,” see [https://developer.android.com/studio/run/oem-usb]).
  4. Verify that [Flutter] can detect the phone: it should appear in the list displayed by the following command, along with the [android] platform:

The phone will access the [NestJS] server via the computer’s IP address on the local network (not via [localhost]): this configuration is described in Chapter 5.

docs.title: 8. The RdvMedecins server, a black box
docs.text:
Examples 22 through 25, followed by the case study, interact with a server: the JSON server of the [RdvMedecins] application. This is the [NestJS] server for courses [React], [Vue.js], and [Angular]: the server for course [NestJS], whose controllers no longer generate HTML pages but instead produce JSON responses. Readers of these lectures are already familiar with this chapter, which is reproduced here almost unchanged; they need only focus on the section on authentication, which explains what changes for a mobile application.

In this course, this server is a black box: you don’t need to know how it’s written. All that matters is its API—that is, the list of HTTP requests it accepts and the responses it returns. This is the typical situation for a client developer: the API is a contract, and the server team can change whatever they want behind that contract. Its source code is provided ([rdvmedecins-nestjs-json] folder) and extensively commented, for the curious reader.

This chapter explains how to install the server, describes its API, and queries it using [curl].

docs.title: 8.1. The RdvMedecins Application
docs.text:
The application manages appointments for a medical practice. It has three roles:

RoleWhoWhat they can do[ADMIN]The administrator ([admin])Schedule and cancel appointments for all patients; manage doctors and clients[DOCTOR]Doctors ([pelissier], [tatou], [dupont])Schedule and cancel appointments for all patients; view all names in the calendars[USER]Patients ([martin], [durand], [bistrou], [german])book appointments for themselves; cancel their appointments; manage their accounts. In a calendar, they cannot see the names of other patients

Demo accounts use their login as the password. The management rules are verified by the server, regardless of the client:

  • no appointments in the past;
  • only one upcoming appointment per patient;
  • a time slot can only be booked once per day;
  • two doctors (or two clients) cannot have the same first and last names; a login belongs to only one account;
  • a doctor with appointments cannot be deleted;
  • A record that has been modified in the meantime by someone else cannot be overwritten (optimistic lock);
  • a patient is never assigned the name of another patient.

docs.title: 8.2. Installation
docs.text:
You need [Node.js] and a [MySQL] (or [MariaDB]) server: their installation is described in the appendix.

  1. The database. The script [database/dbrdvmedecins2.sql] creates the database [dbrdvmedecins2], its tables, and its sample data. Using [Laragon], run it from within [HeidiSQL] (File menu / Run a SQL file); at the command line:
mysql -u root -p < database/dbrdvmedecins2.sql

The script always starts with an empty database: you can rerun it to restore the initial data.

  1. Libraries. In a console window open to the [rdvmedecins-nestjs-json] folder:
npm install
  1. Configuration. Copy the file [.env.example] to [.env] (under [Windows]: [copy .env.example .env]), then modify it:
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sample configuration file.
# Copy this file to [.env] then adapt the values to your machine.
# The [.env] file must never be shared or committed (passwords).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------

# listening port of the JSON server
PORT=8080

# connection parameters for the MySQL database [dbrdvmedecins2]
# (script: database/dbrdvmedecins2.sql)
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=3306
DB_USERNAME=root
DB_PASSWORD=
DB_DATABASE=dbrdvmedecins2
# true: displays in the console the SQL queries sent to MySQL
DB_LOGGING=false

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# authentication
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# secret key used to sign/verify JWT tokens - MUST be changed
# in production (a long random string, never committed).
JWT_SECRET=change-me-to-a-long-random-string
# validity of a JWT token, in seconds (7200 s = 2 h). The cookie
# that carries the token has the same lifetime.
JWT_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS=7200
# set to true in production (site served over HTTPS): the authentication
# cookie will then never be sent over an unencrypted connection.
COOKIE_SECURE=false

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# protection against bots
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# login: number of failures (wrong captcha or password) allowed for
# the same login from the same IP address, before this pair is blocked...
LOGIN_MAX_FAILURES=5
# ... for this duration (an IP address is also blocked if it accumulates
# 5 times more failures, all logins combined)
LOGIN_BLOCK_MINUTES=15
# client account creation: maximum number of accounts created per hour
# from the same IP address. In a classroom, all computers often go out
# through the same address: increase if needed.
REGISTRATION_MAX_PER_HOUR=10

# captcha TEST MODE: if this variable has a value, that value is
# accepted as the answer to ANY captcha. Handy to query
# the API with curl (you cannot "read" the image in a console).
# Leave EMPTY in production.
CAPTCHA_TEST=

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# production
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# folder of the compiled web client, served by this server (default: client/)
# CLIENT_DIR=client
# set to true if the server is behind a proxy (nginx...)
TRUST_PROXY=false
  • line 8: the server listens on port 8080;
  • lines 12–16: the connection to [MySQL]. With [Laragon], the user [root] has no password: the default values are fine;
  • line 25: the secret key that signs the authentication tokens;
  • lines 38–45: anti-bot measures (lockout after multiple failed login attempts, number of accounts created per hour);
  • Line 51: Captcha test mode. The login page requires you to type the characters from an image, which is impossible from a console. If this variable has a value, that value is accepted as the answer to any CAPTCHA, similar to the “test keys” that [Google] provides for its [reCAPTCHA]. For the tests with [curl] in this chapter, enter [CAPTCHA_TEST=test]. The automated tests that generated the screenshots for this course also use this value. Leave it EMPTY in production;
  • lines 57–59: two settings for production (see the “Deployment” chapter).
  1. Launch.
npm run start:dev

The console displays (excerpt):

[Nest] LOG [NestFactory] Starting Nest application...
[Nest] WARN [RdvMedecins] captcha TEST MODE active (CAPTCHA_TEST in .env): never use it in production
[Nest] LOG [RoutesResolver] ScheduleController {/api/schedule}:
[Nest] LOG [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/api/schedule, GET} route
[Nest] LOG [RoutesResolver] AppointmentsController {/api/appointments}:
...
[Nest] LOG [NestApplication] Nest application successfully started
[Nest] LOG [RdvMedecins] JSON server started: http://localhost:8080/api

If the database is inaccessible ([MySQL] server stopped, incorrect password), the server stops immediately with a connection error message.

docs.title: 8.3. Response Format
docs.text:
All URLs begin with [/api]. A successful request receives a 2xx status code and, in its body, the requested data in JSON format. A rejected request receives a 4xx or 5xx code and, in the body, an object that ALWAYS has the same format:

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "key": "ERRORS.INVALID_FORM",
  "params": { "min": "6" },
  "fields": { "lastName": "ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED", "password": "ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT" }
}
  • [statusCode]: the code HTTP, repeated in the body;
  • [key]: the message translation key. The server never returns text to be displayed: it no longer knows the user’s language. It is the client that translates the key using its dictionaries (see Example 21);
  • [params] (optional): the message parameters ([At least {min} characters], [Try again in {minutes} minute(s)]);
  • [fields] (optional): for a rejected form, the error for each field.

Codes used:

CodeMeaningExamples of keys400Invalid request[ERRORS.INVALID_FORM] (+ fields), [ERRORS.INVALID_DATE], [ERRORS.WRONG_CAPTCHA], [ERRORS.CHOOSE_PATIENT], [ERRORS.WRONG_CURRENT_PASSWORD], [ERRORS.BAD_REQUEST]...401not authenticated[ERRORS.AUTH_REQUIRED] (no token), [ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED] (invalid or expired token), [LOGIN.ERROR]403Access Denied[ERRORS.FORBIDDEN] (insufficient role), [ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT] (no pass)404Not found[ERRORS.NOT_FOUND], [ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND], [ERRORS.APPOINTMENT_NOT_FOUND]...409Business rule violation[ERRORS.PAST_DATE], [ERRORS.SLOT_ALREADY_BOOKED], [ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN], [ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE]...415POST, which is not in JSON[ERRORS.JSON_REQUIRED]429Too many attempts[ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS], [ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ACCOUNTS] (+ params.minutes)500server error[ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR]

docs.title: 8.4. Authentication
docs.text:
The client authenticates using [POST /api/auth/login], with a username, password, and CAPTCHA response. In return, the server sends, in the [Set-Cookie] header of its response, a cookie containing a signed token JWT:

Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...; Max-Age=7200; Path=/api; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict

The client must then include this cookie, in the [Cookie] header, with every request to [/api]: this is how the server knows who is making the request.

This server was designed for web clients, and its design choices are driven by the risks specific to web browsers:

  • [HttpOnly]: The page’s code ([JavaScript]) CANNOT read this cookie. A malicious script injected into the page would therefore be unable to steal the token. Consequence for the client: it cannot determine on its own whether it is logged in. It asks the server ([GET /api/auth/me]);
  • [Path=/api]: The cookie is only included in requests to API;
  • [SameSite=Strict]: The browser attaches the cookie only to requests sent to a page on this site. A malicious page on another site cannot cause the browser to act on the user’s behalf (a so-called CSRF attack);
  • [Max-Age=7200]: It expires after two hours, at the same time the token expires.

A second safeguard against CSRF attacks: the server rejects (415) any POST request whose body is not in JSON. A compromised HTML form on another site cannot send JSON.

What about a mobile app? There is no browser: no one stores the cookie or sends it back on its own. The app will take on this role by reading the [Set-Cookie] header in the responses and writing the [Cookie] header in the requests (example 23). The attributes [HttpOnly] and [SameSite] apply only to browsers: they have no effect on the app, just as [curl] does not. The same [Flutter] application, when compiled for the web, will, however, function as browsers do: the cookie is managed by the browser, provided that the application and API share the same origin (see Example 22 and the “Deployment” chapter).

docs.title: 8.5. The API
docs.text:
MethodAddressRolesSent/Response BodyGET[/api/captcha]publicResponse: [{ id, svg }]POST[/api/auth/login]public[{ login, password, captchaId, captcha }]; response: [{ login, name, role }] + cookiePOST[/api/auth/logout]public[{}] ; deletes the cookieGET[/api/auth/me]logged inresponse: [{ login, name, role }]GET[/api/schedule?doctorId=&day=]allAnswer: the calendar (without doctorId: for a DOCTOR, his own)POST[/api/appointments]all[{ day, slotId, clientId }] (clientId ignored for a USER); 201DELETE[/api/appointments/:id]allA USER cancels only its ownGET[/api/doctors]allthe list (with login for ADMIN)GET[/api/clients]ADMIN, DOCTORthe list (with login for ADMIN)GET[/api/doctors/:id], [/api/clients/:id]ADMINa recordPOST[/api/doctors], [/api/clients]ADMIN[{ title, firstName, lastName, login?, password? }]; 201PUT[/api/doctors/:id], [/api/clients/:id]ADMIN[{ title, firstName, lastName, login?, password?, version }]DELETE[/api/doctors/:id], [/api/clients/:id]ADMINAnswer: [{}]POST[/api/register/access]public[{ captchaId, captcha }]; issues a token (cookie)GET[/api/register/access]publicresponse: [{ valid }]POST[/api/register]public + pass[{ title, firstName, lastName, login, password, confirmation }]; 201GET[/api/my-area]USERresponse: [{ patient, appointments }]GET[/api/my-account]USERResponse: [{ title, firstName, lastName, login, version }]PUT[/api/my-account]USER[{ title, firstName, lastName, login, password?, confirmation?, currentPassword, version }]DELETE[/api/my-account]USER[{ currentPassword }]; deletes the account and its appointments

A calendar entry ([GET /api/schedule]) describes a time slot AND what the logged-in user is authorized to do with it:

{ "id": 3, "startHour": 8, "startMinute": 40, "endHour": 9, "endMinute": 0,
  "free": false,
  "patient": { "title": "Mme", "firstName": "Alice", "lastName": "DURAND" },
  "mine": false, "bookable": false, "appointmentId": 2 }
  • [free]: Is the time slot available on that day?
  • [patient]: the patient for the appointment. For a logged-in patient, this is equal to [null], except for THEIR OWN appointment: the names of other patients are never sent;
  • [mine]: This is the logged-in patient’s appointment;
  • [bookable]: Can the user book this time slot (available, not in the past, and, for a patient, no upcoming appointments)?
  • [appointmentId]: filled in if the user can cancel this appointment.

The server DECIDES; the client displays. And even if a client were to cheat (by displaying a “Book” button when it shouldn’t), the server would double-check everything at the time of booking.

docs.title: 8.6. Query the API using curl
docs.text:
The [curl] folder on the server contains the JSON request bodies from this chapter, with one file per request. For example, [curl/login-admin.json]:

{ "login": "admin", "password": "admin", "captchaId": "-", "captcha": "test" }

Commands are entered in a console opened on the [rdvmedecins-nestjs-json] directory. Some options for [curl]:

  • [-i]: also display the response headers; [-s]: without a progress bar;
  • [--json @file]: send the contents of the file in POST, with the header [Content-Type: application/json] (curl 7.82 and later; with an older version, use [-H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @file]);
  • [-X PUT], [-X DELETE]: the HTTP method;
  • [-c cookies.txt]: save the received cookies to this file; [-b cookies.txt]: send them back. This is how [curl] “stays logged in” from one command to the next, just as a browser would.

Under [PowerShell], you must enter [curl.exe] and not [curl] (which refers to a different command there). The somewhat lengthy responses for JSON have been formatted for this document, and the headers for [Date], [ETag], [Connection], and [Keep-Alive] have been removed.

docs.title: 8.6.1. Login
docs.text:
First, the CAPTCHA (the image is cropped):

$ curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/captcha
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Cache-Control: no-store
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 11428

{"id": "968678a8-25f0-4892-9fc4-bd93533dab33", "svg": "<svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" width=\"150..."}

Without a token, a protected URL returns a 401 response:

$ curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/doctors
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 47

{"statusCode": 401, "key": "ERRORS.AUTH_REQUIRED"}

An incorrect CAPTCHA, followed by an incorrect password:

$ curl -i --json @curl/login-wrong-captcha.json http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 91

{"statusCode": 400, "key": "ERRORS.WRONG_CAPTCHA", "fields": {"captcha": "ERRORS.WRONG_CAPTCHA"}}

$ curl -i --json @curl/login-wrong-password.json http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 38

{"statusCode": 401, "key": "LOGIN.ERROR"}

A successful login sets the cookie, which [curl] stores in [cookies.txt]:

$ curl -i -c cookies.txt --json @curl/login-admin.json http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...; Max-Age=7200; Path=/api; Expires=Mon, 28 Sep 2026 12:49:12 GMT; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 55

{"login": "admin", "name": "Administrator", "role": "ADMIN"}

With this cookie, the server knows who we are:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt http://localhost:8080/api/auth/me
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 55

{"login": "admin", "name": "Administrator", "role": "ADMIN"}

A forged (or expired) token results in an expired session, and the server instructs the browser to delete the cookie:

$ curl -i -b "rdvmedecins_jwt=abc.def.ghi" http://localhost:8080/api/auth/me
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=; Path=/api; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 49

{"statusCode": 401, "key": "ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED"}

docs.title: 8.6.2. Doctors, clients, calendar
docs.text:
The list of doctors, as seen by ADMIN (with logins):

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt http://localhost:8080/api/doctors
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 282

[
  {"id": 3, "version": 0, "title": "Melle", "firstName": "Sophie", "lastName": "DUPONT", "login": "dupont"},
  {"id": 1, "version": 0, "title": "Mme", "firstName": "Marie", "lastName": "PELISSIER", "login": "pelissier"},
  {"id": 2, "version": 0, "title": "Mr", "firstName": "Paul", "lastName": "TATOU", "login": "tatou"}

{"statusCode": 400, "key": "ERRORS.INVALID_DATE"}

docs.title: 8.6.3. Appointments
docs.text:
ADMIN reserves slot 3 for patient No. 2 (Alice DURAND). The body of the request:

{ "day": "2030-01-15", "slotId": 3, "clientId": 2 }

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt --json @curl/appointment-admin.json http://localhost:8080/api/appointments
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 51

{"id": 2, "day": "2030-01-15", "slotId": 3, "clientId": 2}

The calendar now displays this appointment, along with the patient’s name and instructions on how to cancel it ([appointmentId]):

$ curl -s -b cookies.txt "http://localhost:8080/api/schedule?doctorId=1&day=2030-01-15"
{
  "doctor": {"id": 1, "version": 0, "title": "Mme", "firstName": "Marie", "lastName": "PELISSIER"},
  "day": "2030-01-15",

    {"id": 3, "startHour": 8, "startMinute": 40, "endHour": 9, "endMinute": 0, "free": false, "patient": {"title": "Mme", "firstName": "Alice", "lastName": "DURAND"}, "mine": false, "bookable": false, "appointmentId": 2},
    {"id": 4, "startHour": 9, "startMinute": 0, "endHour": 9, "endMinute": 20, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 5, "startHour": 9, "startMinute": 20, "endHour": 9, "endMinute": 40, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 6, "startHour": 9, "startMinute": 40, "endHour": 10, "endMinute": 0, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 7, "startHour": 10, "startMinute": 0, "endHour": 10, "endMinute": 20, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 8, "startHour": 10, "startMinute": 20, "endHour": 10, "endMinute": 40, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 9, "startHour": 10, "startMinute": 40, "endHour": 11, "endMinute": 0, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 10, "startHour": 11, "startMinute": 0, "endHour": 11, "endMinute": 20, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 11, "startHour": 11, "startMinute": 20, "endHour": 11, "endMinute": 40, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},

  ],
  "info": null
}

Try again: the patient already has an upcoming appointment. An appointment in the past is also rejected:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt --json @curl/appointment-admin.json http://localhost:8080/api/appointments
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 66

{"statusCode": 409, "key": "ERRORS.PATIENT_HAS_UPCOMING_APPOINTMENT"}

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt --json @curl/appointment-past.json http://localhost:8080/api/appointments
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 43

{"statusCode": 409, "key": "ERRORS.PAST_DATE"}

A standard HTML form (simulated here by [-d], which sends [application/x-www-form-urlencoded]) is rejected:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -d "day=2030-01-15&slotId=4&clientId=2" http://localhost:8080/api/appointments
HTTP/1.1 415 Unsupported Media Type
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 47

{"statusCode": 415, "key": "ERRORS.JSON_REQUIRED"}

docs.title: 8.6.4. A patient’s perspective
docs.text:
You log out, then log in as [martin]:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -c cookies.txt --json @curl/empty.json http://localhost:8080/api/auth/logout
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=; Path=/api; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 2

{}

$ curl -s -c cookies-martin.txt --json @curl/login-martin.json http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login
{"login": "martin", "name": "Jean MARTIN", "role": "USER"}

The same schedule, as seen by a patient: slot 3 is occupied (["free": false]), but ["patient"] is equivalent to [null]: Alice’s name, DURAND, was not sent:

$ curl -s -b cookies-martin.txt "http://localhost:8080/api/schedule?doctorId=1&day=2030-01-15"
{
  "doctor": {"id": 1, "version": 0, "title": "Mme", "firstName": "Marie", "lastName": "PELISSIER"},
  "day": "2030-01-15",
  "slots": [
    {"id": 1, "startHour": 8, "startMinute": 0, "endHour": 8, "endMinute": 20, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 2, "startHour": 8, "startMinute": 20, "endHour": 8, "endMinute": 40, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 3, "startHour": 8, "startMinute": 40, "endHour": 9, "endMinute": 0, "free": false, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": false, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 4, "startHour": 9, "startMinute": 0, "endHour": 9, "endMinute": 20, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 5, "startHour": 9, "startMinute": 20, "endHour": 9, "endMinute": 40, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 6, "startHour": 9, "startMinute": 40, "endHour": 10, "endMinute": 0, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 7, "startHour": 10, "startMinute": 0, "endHour": 10, "endMinute": 20, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 8, "startHour": 10, "startMinute": 20, "endHour": 10, "endMinute": 40, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 9, "startHour": 10, "startMinute": 40, "endHour": 11, "endMinute": 0, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 10, "startHour": 11, "startMinute": 0, "endHour": 11, "endMinute": 20, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 11, "startHour": 11, "startMinute": 20, "endHour": 11, "endMinute": 40, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 12, "startHour": 11, "startMinute": 40, "endHour": 12, "endMinute": 0, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null}
  ],
  "info": null
}

A patient does not have access to the client list:

$ curl -i -b cookies-martin.txt http://localhost:8080/api/clients
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 43

{"statusCode": 403, "key": "ERRORS.FORBIDDEN"}

They are making a reservation for themselves (the body does not contain [clientId]), once, not twice:

{ "day": "2030-01-15", "slotId": 5 }

$ curl -i -b cookies-martin.txt --json @curl/appointment-martin.json http://localhost:8080/api/appointments
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 51

{"id": 3, "day": "2030-01-15", "slotId": 5, "clientId": 1}

$ curl -i -b cookies-martin.txt --json @curl/appointment-martin-2.json http://localhost:8080/api/appointments
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 55

{"statusCode": 409, "key": "SCHEDULE.ALREADY_BOOKED_INFO"}

His area:

$ curl -s -b cookies-martin.txt http://localhost:8080/api/my-area
{
  "patient": {"title": "Mr", "firstName": "Jean", "lastName": "MARTIN"},
  "appointments": [
    {
      "id": 3,
      "day": "2030-01-15",
      "slot": {"id": 5, "startHour": 9, "startMinute": 20, "endHour": 9, "endMinute": 40},
      "doctor": {"id": 1, "version": 0, "title": "Mme", "firstName": "Marie", "lastName": "PELISSIER"}
    }
  ]
}

He cannot cancel another patient’s appointment. The server responds with “not found,” just as it would for an appointment that does not exist: it reveals nothing about other patients’ appointments:

$ curl -i -b cookies-martin.txt -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/api/appointments/2
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 55

{"statusCode": 404, "key": "ERRORS.APPOINTMENT_NOT_FOUND"}

His own, yes:

$ curl -i -b cookies-martin.txt -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/api/appointments/3
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 2

{}

docs.title: 8.6.5. A doctor’s perspective
docs.text:
