$ curl -s -b cookies-pelissier.txt "http://localhost:8080/api/schedule?day=2030-01-15"
{
  "doctor": {"id": 1, "version": 0, "title": "Mme", "firstName": "Marie", "lastName": "PELISSIER"},
  "day": "2030-01-15",
  "slots": [
    {"id": 1, "startHour": 8, "startMinute": 0, "endHour": 8, "endMinute": 20, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 2, "startHour": 8, "startMinute": 20, "endHour": 8, "endMinute": 40, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 3, "startHour": 8, "startMinute": 40, "endHour": 9, "endMinute": 0, "free": false, "patient": {"title": "Mme", "firstName": "Alice", "lastName": "DURAND"}, "mine": false, "bookable": false, "appointmentId": 2},
    {"id": 4, "startHour": 9, "startMinute": 0, "endHour": 9, "endMinute": 20, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 5, "startHour": 9, "startMinute": 20, "endHour": 9, "endMinute": 40, "free": false, "patient": {"title": "Mr", "firstName": "Jean", "lastName": "MARTIN"}, "mine": false, "bookable": false, "appointmentId": 3},
    {"id": 6, "startHour": 9, "startMinute": 40, "endHour": 10, "endMinute": 0, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 7, "startHour": 10, "startMinute": 0, "endHour": 10, "endMinute": 20, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 8, "startHour": 10, "startMinute": 20, "endHour": 10, "endMinute": 40, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 9, "startHour": 10, "startMinute": 40, "endHour": 11, "endMinute": 0, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 10, "startHour": 11, "startMinute": 0, "endHour": 11, "endMinute": 20, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 11, "startHour": 11, "startMinute": 20, "endHour": 11, "endMinute": 40, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null},
    {"id": 12, "startHour": 11, "startMinute": 40, "endHour": 12, "endMinute": 0, "free": true, "patient": null, "mine": false, "bookable": true, "appointmentId": null}
  ],
  "info": null
}

It does not manage doctors:

$ curl -i -b cookies-pelissier.txt --json @curl/doctor-add.json http://localhost:8080/api/doctors
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 43

{"statusCode": 403, "key": "ERRORS.FORBIDDEN"}

docs.title: 8.6.6. Managing doctors and clients (ADMIN)
docs.text:
An addition. If the username is missing, the default is the name in lowercase; the password is the username:

{ "title": "Mme", "firstName": "Claire", "lastName": "LEROY" }

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt --json @curl/doctor-add.json http://localhost:8080/api/doctors
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 90

{"id": 4, "version": 1, "title": "Mme", "firstName": "Claire", "lastName": "LEROY", "login": "leroy"}

Invalid body: the response lists the error for each field:

{ "title": "Dr", "firstName": "", "lastName": "A-LAST-NAME-FAR-TOO-LONG-FOR-THE-DB", "login": "Claire L" }

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt --json @curl/doctor-invalid.json http://localhost:8080/api/doctors
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 218

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "key": "ERRORS.INVALID_FORM",
  "params": {"min": "6"},
  "fields": {"login": "ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN", "title": "ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE", "firstName": "ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_REQUIRED", "lastName": "ERRORS.LASTNAME_TOO_LONG"}
}

A homonym: both affected fields are flagged:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt --json @curl/doctor-duplicate.json http://localhost:8080/api/doctors
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 151

{"statusCode": 409, "key": "ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS", "fields": {"firstName": "ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS", "lastName": "ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS"}}

A modification. The [version] is the one read from the record (here, 1):

{ "title": "Mme", "firstName": "Claire", "lastName": "LEROY-MARTIN", "version": 1 }

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -X PUT --json @curl/doctor-edit.json http://localhost:8080/api/doctors/4
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 97

{"id": 4, "version": 2, "title": "Mme", "firstName": "Claire", "lastName": "LEROY-MARTIN", "login": "leroy"}

The record is now at version 2. Resubmitting the same change (with version 1) would overwrite a record that has since been modified by someone else: the optimistic lock prevents this:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -X PUT --json @curl/doctor-edit.json http://localhost:8080/api/doctors/4
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 51

{"statusCode": 409, "key": "ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE"}

A doctor with appointments cannot be deleted; the others can:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/api/doctors/1
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 57

{"statusCode": 409, "key": "ERRORS.DOCTOR_HAS_APPOINTMENTS"}

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/api/doctors/4
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 2

{}

docs.title: 8.6.7. Creating an account
docs.text:
Without a pass, it’s impossible:

$ curl -i --json @curl/registration.json http://localhost:8080/api/register
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 56

{"statusCode": 403, "key": "ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT"}

First, you solve a CAPTCHA; the server issues a token, valid for 15 minutes, in a cookie:

$ curl -i -c cookies-registration.txt --json @curl/captcha-test.json http://localhost:8080/api/register/access
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_registration=60f5fa35-f939-4c87-b5a2-7c2f38054cc3; Max-Age=900; Path=/api/register; Expires=Mon, 28 Sep 2026 11:04:12 GMT; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 2

{}

$ curl -s -b cookies-registration.txt http://localhost:8080/api/register/access
{"valid": true}

The password confirmation must be identical:

$ curl -i -b cookies-registration.txt --json @curl/registration-confirmation.json http://localhost:8080/api/register
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 98

{"statusCode": 400, "key": "ERRORS.INVALID_FORM", "fields": {"confirmation": "ERRORS.PASSWORDS_DIFFER"}}

{ "title": "Mme", "firstName": "Julie", "lastName": "BERNARD", "login": "jbernard", "password": "secret1", "confirmation": "secret1" }

$ curl -i -b cookies-registration.txt -c cookies-registration.txt --json @curl/registration.json http://localhost:8080/api/register
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_registration=; Path=/api/register; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 20

{"login": "jbernard"}

The passcode has been used: it cannot be used to create a second account:

$ curl -i -b cookies-registration.txt --json @curl/registration.json http://localhost:8080/api/register
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 56

{"statusCode": 403, "key": "ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT"}

docs.title: 8.6.8. Manage Your Account
docs.text:
The new patient logs in and reads her account record:

$ curl -s -b cookies-jbernard.txt http://localhost:8080/api/my-account
{"title": "Mme", "firstName": "Julie", "lastName": "BERNARD", "login": "jbernard", "version": 1}

Making a change requires the current password. The server issues a new token, which contains the new name:

{ "title": "Mme", "firstName": "Julie", "lastName": "BERNARD-DUVAL", "login": "jbernard", "currentPassword": "secret1", "version": 1 }

$ curl -i -b cookies-jbernard.txt -c cookies-jbernard.txt -X PUT --json @curl/my-account.json http://localhost:8080/api/my-account
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...; Max-Age=7200; Path=/api; Expires=Mon, 28 Sep 2026 12:49:13 GMT; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 63

{"login": "jbernard", "name": "Julie BERNARD-DUVAL", "role": "USER"}

Deleting the account also deletes the cookie:

$ curl -i -b cookies-jbernard.txt -c cookies-jbernard.txt -X DELETE --json @curl/my-account-delete.json http://localhost:8080/api/my-account
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=; Path=/api; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 2

{}

$ curl -i -b cookies-jbernard.txt http://localhost:8080/api/auth/me
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 47

{"statusCode": 401, "key": "ERRORS.AUTH_REQUIRED"}

docs.title: 8.6.9. Some errors
docs.text:
An unknown route, a body that is not a valid JSON:

$ curl -i -b cookies-martin.txt http://localhost:8080/api/does-not-exist
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 43

{"statusCode": 404, "key": "ERRORS.NOT_FOUND"}

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{not json" http://localhost:8080/api/appointments
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 45

{"statusCode": 400, "key": "ERRORS.BAD_REQUEST"}

We now know everything we need to know about the server to write our client.

docs.title: 4. Widgets
docs.text: Writing your own widgets is at the heart of working with [Flutter]: a well-written screen is made up of small widgets, each with its own parameters, its [build], and, if necessary, its state. This chapter shows how they communicate with each other (parameters, functions), how they are assembled (composition), how they function (lifecycle), how they share data without passing it from one to another (inherited data), and how to reuse behavior.

docs.title: 4.1.1. Data Type
docs.text:
The parent and child share a class, defined in its own file:

// the data type shared by the parent (DoctorsPage) and the child (DoctorCard)
class Doctor {
  final int id;
  final String title;
  final String firstName;
  final String lastName;
  final String specialty;
  final bool available;

  const Doctor({
    required this.id,
    required this.title,
    required this.firstName,
    required this.lastName,
    required this.specialty,
    required this.available,
  });

  // a copy in which only the availability changes
  Doctor withAvailability(bool d) =>
      Doctor(id: id, title: title, firstName: firstName, lastName: lastName, specialty: specialty, available: d);
}
  • lines 10–16: a constructor with named parameters, all of which are required: [Doctor(id: 1, title: 'Mme', ...)]. Named parameters make the call readable, and their order does not matter;
  • lines 20–21: a copy where only the availability changes (the object itself never changes).

docs.title: 4.1.2. The child
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex10_widget_parameters/doctor_card.dart - a CHILD widget
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// It receives its data from its parent through the PARAMETERS of its
// constructor, stored in final fields. Their type is checked at
// compile time: DoctorCard(doctor: 42) would be refused.
//   - required: the parent MUST provide this parameter;
//   - this.compact = false: an optional parameter, with its default value.
//
// Golden rule: a widget NEVER MODIFIES its parameters (they are final).
// The data go down from the parent to the child; to request a
// change, the child calls a function that the parent passed to it
// (see example 11). When the parent changes its data, it REBUILDS its
// children with new parameters.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

import 'doctor.dart';

// the "style" of the card: constants PRIVATE to this file (the "_").
// No other widget can see them, nor be bothered by them
const _initialsColor = Color(0xFF087EA4);
const _initialsStyle = TextStyle(color: Colors.white, fontWeight: FontWeight.bold);

class DoctorCard extends StatelessWidget {
  final Doctor doctor;
  final int rank;
  final bool compact;

  // const: if all the parameters are constant, the widget is too
  // (Flutter then does not even need to rebuild it)
  const DoctorCard({super.key, required this.doctor, required this.rank, this.compact = false});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    // a value computed from the parameters
    final initials = '${doctor.firstName[0]}${doctor.lastName[0]}';

    return Card(
      // a green border for an available doctor
      shape: RoundedRectangleBorder(
        borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(12),
        side: doctor.available ? const BorderSide(color: Colors.green, width: 2) : BorderSide.none,
      ),
      child: Padding(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
        child: Row(
          children: [
            CircleAvatar(
              backgroundColor: _initialsColor,
              child: Text(initials, style: _initialsStyle),
            ),
            const SizedBox(width: 12),
            // Expanded: the text takes all the remaining width
            Expanded(
              child: Column(
                crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
                children: [
                  Text(
                    '$rank. ${doctor.title} ${doctor.firstName} ${doctor.lastName}',
                    style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleMedium,
                  ),
                  if (!compact) Text(doctor.specialty, style: const TextStyle(color: Colors.grey)),
                ],
              ),
            ),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • lines 23–24: the card’s “style”: constants private to this file (the “_”). No other file can see them or be affected by them. This is the equivalent, in [Flutter], of the “CSS modules” in [React]: there is no global stylesheet; a widget’s style is embedded in its code;
  • lines 27–29: the widget’s parameters, stored in [final] fields;
  • line 33: the constructor. [required this.doctor]: a required parameter, stored directly in the field; [this.compact = false]: an optional parameter, with its default value. The constructor is [const]: if all arguments are constant, the card is also constant;
  • line 38: a value calculated from the parameters;
  • lines 42–44: the card’s shape ([Card]): rounded corners and a green border if a doctor is available ([BorderSide.none] otherwise);
  • lines 50–52: a colored disc with the initials;
  • line 64: the specialty is only displayed in non-compact view.

Golden rule: a widget never modifies its own parameters (they are [final]; the compiler prohibits this, by the way). Data flows from the parent to the child; to request a change, the child calls a function passed to it by the parent (Example 11). When the parent changes its data, it reconstructs its children with new parameters.

docs.title: 4.1.3. The parent
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex10_widget_parameters/main.dart - the PARENT widget
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// It imports the DoctorCard widget and uses it, as many times as
// needed, like any Flutter widget: a widget is a piece
// of REUSABLE interface, with its own parameters, its build() and
// its style. Writing your own widgets is the heart of working with
// Flutter: a well-written screen is made of small widgets.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

import 'doctor_card.dart';
import 'doctor.dart';

void main() {
  runApp(
    MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      home: const DoctorsPage(),
    ),
  );
}

class DoctorsPage extends StatefulWidget {
  const DoctorsPage({super.key});

  @override
  State<DoctorsPage> createState() => _DoctorsPageState();
}

class _DoctorsPageState extends State<DoctorsPage> {
  List<Doctor> _doctors = const [
    Doctor(id: 1, title: 'Mme', firstName: 'Marie', lastName: 'PELISSIER', specialty: 'general practitioner', available: true),
    Doctor(id: 2, title: 'Mr', firstName: 'Paul', lastName: 'TATOU', specialty: 'pediatrician', available: false),
    Doctor(id: 3, title: 'Melle', firstName: 'Sophie', lastName: 'DUPONT', specialty: 'general practitioner', available: true),
  ];
  bool _compact = false;

  // the parent changes ITS data: Flutter calls its build() again, which
  // rebuilds the children with their new parameters
  void _toggleAvailability() {
    setState(() {
      _doctors = [for (final m in _doctors) m.withAvailability(!m.available)];
    });
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Example 10 - the widgets and their parameters')),
      body: ListView(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
        children: [
          SwitchListTile(
            contentPadding: EdgeInsets.zero,
            title: const Text('compact display'),
            value: _compact,
            onChanged: (v) => setState(() => _compact = v),
          ),
          Align(
            alignment: Alignment.centerLeft,
            child: OutlinedButton(onPressed: _toggleAvailability, child: const Text('Toggle the availabilities')),
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 8),
          for (final (i, m) in _doctors.indexed)
            // each card receives ITS parameters
            DoctorCard(key: ValueKey(m.id), doctor: m, rank: i + 1, compact: _compact),
          const SizedBox(height: 16),
          const Text(
            'The same card, in its compact version, by setting the parameter:',
            style: TextStyle(color: Colors.grey),
          ),
          SizedBox(width: 260, child: DoctorCard(doctor: _doctors[0], rank: 1, compact: true)),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • lines 34–39: the parent’s state: the list of doctors (a constant list, which will be replaced by another) and the compact display;
  • lines 43–45: the parent changes ITS data to a new list consisting of copies of the doctors. [Flutter] calls its [build], which rebuilds the cards with their new parameters;
  • line 69: one card per doctor, with ITS parameters. The [DoctorCard] widget is used exactly like a [Flutter] widget;
  • line 75: the same card, in a compact version, in a box 260 points wide.

Initially, then in compact view, availability is reversed:

A method that creates widgets (like [_line] from Example 02) or a real widget ([DoctorCard])? The actual widget is almost always preferable: it has a name, its parameters are typed and documented, it can be reused elsewhere, and [Flutter] can avoid rebuilding it (if it is [const], or if its parameters haven’t changed).

docs.title: 4.2. Example 11: The child notifies its parent
docs.text: Data flows down through parameters; information flows back up through functions passed as parameters.

docs.title: 4.2.1. "Events" from the child
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex11_lifting_state_up/counter.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A child that NOTIFIES its parent: the parent passes it FUNCTIONS as
// parameters (by convention, their name starts with "on"), and the child
// calls them when something happens:
//     Counter(label: 'Coffees', max: 3, onIncrement: ..., onLimit: ...)
// The types of these functions have ready-made names in Flutter:
//   - ValueChanged<int> : a function that receives an int and returns nothing;
//   - VoidCallback      : a function without parameters, that returns nothing.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

class Counter extends StatefulWidget {
  final String label;
  final int max;
  final ValueChanged<int> onIncrement; // with the new value
  final VoidCallback onLimit; // without data

  const Counter({
    super.key,
    required this.label,
    required this.max,
    required this.onIncrement,
    required this.onLimit,
  });

  @override
  State<Counter> createState() => _CounterState();
}

class _CounterState extends State<Counter> {
  // the state SPECIFIC to this counter: each Counter has its own
  int _value = 0;

  void _plus() {
    // widget: in the State object, gives access to the parameters of the widget
    if (_value >= widget.max) {
      widget.onLimit();
      return;
    }
    setState(() => _value++);
    // the parent is NOTIFIED, and receives the new value
    widget.onIncrement(_value);
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Row(
      children: [
        SizedBox(width: 110, child: Text(widget.label)),
        OutlinedButton(onPressed: _plus, child: const Text('+1')),
        const SizedBox(width: 12),
        Chip(label: Text('$_value / ${widget.max}')),
      ],
    );
  }
}
  • lines 18–19: two parameters that are functions, which the counter will call. [ValueChanged<int>] is the type of a function that takes a [int] and returns nothing; [VoidCallback] is the type of a function with no parameters. By convention, their names begin with “on,” such as [onPressed] or [onChanged] for the widgets of [Flutter];
  • line 35: the state SPECIFIC to this counter: each [Counter] has its own;
  • lines 37–45: within the [State] object, [widget] provides access to the widget’s settings: [widget.max], [widget.onLimit]... If the maximum is exceeded, the counter notifies its parent ([widget.onLimit()]); otherwise, it changes its state and then notifies its parent by transmitting the new value. Unlike [React], the state is updated immediately: [_value] already has its new value when it is transmitted.

docs.title: 4.2.2. A controlled widget
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex11_lifting_state_up/labeled_text_field.dart - a CONTROLLED widget
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A "home-made" form field (label + field + help + character
// counter) that is used like a controlled field:
//     LabeledTextField(value: _name, onChanged: (v) => setState(() => _name = v), ...)
// The value belongs to the PARENT, which passes it (value) and which it
// notifies of each keystroke (onChanged). The parent is the one who decides.
//
// A difficulty specific to Flutter: a TextField keeps its text in a
// controller, which must survive the rebuilds. The widget therefore has a
// state (the controller)... which it must keep UP TO DATE when the parent changes
// the value ("Clear" button): that is the role of didUpdateWidget.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

class LabeledTextField extends StatefulWidget {
  final String value;
  final ValueChanged<String> onChanged;
  final String label;
  final int max;
  final String help;

  const LabeledTextField({
    super.key,
    required this.value,
    required this.onChanged,
    required this.label,
    required this.max,
    this.help = '',
  });

  @override
  State<LabeledTextField> createState() => _LabeledTextFieldState();
}

class _LabeledTextFieldState extends State<LabeledTextField> {
  // late: the field will be initialized later (in initState), before any use
  late final TextEditingController _controller;

  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
    _controller = TextEditingController(text: widget.value);
  }

  // called when the PARENT rebuilds this widget with new parameters;
  // oldWidget: the previous widget, to compare
  @override
  void didUpdateWidget(LabeledTextField oldWidget) {
    super.didUpdateWidget(oldWidget);
    if (widget.value != _controller.text) {
      _controller.text = widget.value; // the parent changed the value itself
    }
  }

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _controller.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final full = widget.value.length == widget.max;
    return TextField(
      controller: _controller,
      maxLength: widget.max, // the field refuses the extra characters
      decoration: InputDecoration(
        labelText: widget.label,
        helperText: widget.help,
        // the border becomes red when the field is full
        errorText: full ? 'Maximum length reached' : null,
      ),
      onChanged: widget.onChanged, // the parent's function, passed as is
    );
  }
}

A “custom” form field (label + field + tooltip + character counter) that functions as a controlled field: the value belongs to the parent, which passes it to the field ([value]) and notifies the parent of each keystroke ([onChanged]).

  • Line 40: [late]: This field will be initialized later (in [initState]), but before it is used. [Dart] checks it at runtime;
  • Lines 43–45: The controller starts with the parent’s value;
  • lines 51–54: This is the specific challenge with [Flutter]: a [TextField] stores its text in a controller, which must survive page rebuilds. The widget therefore has a state (the controller)... which it must keep up to date when the parent changes the value itself (Clear button). [didUpdateWidget] is called every time the parent rebuilds this widget with new parameters; it receives the old widget for comparison. If the parent’s value differs from the field’s text, it is copied over;
  • line 69: the field rejects excess characters and displays a counter (“12/20”);
  • line 72: a tooltip appears below the field;
  • line 74: the border turns red when the field is full;
  • line 76: the parent’s function, passed as-is to [TextField].

docs.title: 4.2.3. The parent
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex11_lifting_state_up/main.dart - the parent listens to its children
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The data go down (parameters); the information goes up through
// functions passed as parameters:
//   1. "events" of the child: onIncrement, onLimit;
//   2. a controlled widget: value + onChanged, like a Checkbox. The state
//      remains the property of the parent, which can modify it itself (Clear).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

import 'labeled_text_field.dart';
import 'counter.dart';

void main() {
  runApp(
    MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      home: const ParentPage(),
    ),
  );
}

class ParentPage extends StatefulWidget {
  const ParentPage({super.key});

  @override
  State<ParentPage> createState() => _ParentPageState();
}

class _ParentPageState extends State<ParentPage> {
  int _total = 0;
  String _message = '';
  String _firstName = 'Marie';
  String _lastName = 'PELISSIER';

  // the function called by a counter: it receives the value the counter passes
  void _onIncrement(String label, int value) {
    setState(() {
      _total++;
      _message = '$label is now $value';
    });
  }

  void _clear() {
    setState(() {
      _firstName = '';
      _lastName = '';
    });
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final titleStyle = Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleSmall;
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Example 11 - the child notifies its parent')),
      body: ListView(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
        children: [
          Card(
            child: Padding(
              padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
              child: Column(
                crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
                children: [
                  Text('1. Functions called by the children', style: titleStyle),
                  Counter(
                    label: 'Coffees',
                    max: 3,
                    onIncrement: (v) => _onIncrement('Coffees', v),
                    onLimit: () => setState(() => _message = 'No more than 3 coffees!'),
                  ),
                  Counter(
                    label: 'Glasses of water',
                    max: 8,
                    onIncrement: (v) => _onIncrement('Glasses of water', v),
                    onLimit: () => setState(() => _message = 'Enough drinking.'),
                  ),
                  const SizedBox(height: 8),
                  Text('Total of the clicks: $_total - $_message', style: const TextStyle(fontStyle: FontStyle.italic)),
                ],
              ),
            ),
          ),
          Card(
            child: Padding(
              padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
              child: Column(
                crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
                children: [
                  Text('2. Controlled widgets', style: titleStyle),
                  LabeledTextField(
                    value: _firstName,
                    onChanged: (v) => setState(() => _firstName = v),
                    label: 'First name',
                    max: 20,
                    help: 'Required',
                  ),
                  LabeledTextField(
                    value: _lastName,
                    onChanged: (v) => setState(() => _lastName = v),
                    label: 'Last name',
                    max: 20,
                    help: 'Upper-cased when displayed',
                  ),
                  const SizedBox(height: 8),
                  Text.rich(
                    TextSpan(
                      children: [
                        const TextSpan(text: "Parent's data: "),
                        TextSpan(
                          text: '$_firstName ${_lastName.toUpperCase()}',
                          style: const TextStyle(fontWeight: FontWeight.bold),
                        ),
                      ],
                    ),
                  ),
                  const SizedBox(height: 8),
                  OutlinedButton(onPressed: _clear, child: const Text('Clear (from the parent)')),
                ],
              ),
            ),
          ),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • lines 40–43: the function called by a counter; it receives the value passed by the counter;
  • lines 69–73: a counter and the functions it will call. [(v) => _onIncrement('Coffees', v)]: an anonymous function that adds its own argument (the label);
  • lines 94–99: a controlled field: its value, and the function that changes the parent’s state;
  • line 114: the parent’s data, which follows the entry;
  • Line 121: The parent changes the value themselves: the fields are cleared (via their [didUpdateWidget]).

Press the first counter four times, the second counter once, and enter the name; then clear the fields from the parent:

docs.title: 4.3.1. A card
docs.text:
A widget’s parameters transmit data… but also content: a widget is a value like any other, which can be passed to another widget. [Flutter] uses it everywhere: the [child] of a [Padding], the [title] of a [AppBar], the [body] of a [Scaffold].

// =========================================================================
// lib/ex12_composition/info_card.dart - a reusable TEMPLATE
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The parameters of a widget pass DATA... but also
// CONTENT: a widget is a value like any other, which can be passed to
// another widget, which places it wherever it wants. Flutter uses this everywhere:
// the child of a Padding, the title of an AppBar, the body of a Scaffold...
//   - child: by convention, the "main" content;
//   - header, footer: other places (some "slots"), provided by the
//     parent; the header has a default content, the footer is optional.
// The card sets the frame (border, header, footer), the parent provides what
// goes inside.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

class InfoCard extends StatelessWidget {
  final Color? color; // "?": optional (null by default)
  final Widget header;
  final Widget? footer;
  final Widget child;

  const InfoCard({super.key, this.color, this.header = const Text('Untitled'), this.footer, required this.child});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final background = color ?? Colors.grey.shade300;
    return Card(
      // clipBehavior: the colored header follows the rounded corners of the card
      clipBehavior: Clip.antiAlias,
      shape: RoundedRectangleBorder(
        borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(8),
        side: BorderSide(color: background),
      ),
      child: Column(
        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch,
        children: [
          Container(
            color: background,
            padding: const EdgeInsets.all(10),
            // DefaultTextStyle: the style of ALL the texts of the header,
            // whatever the widget provided by the parent
            child: DefaultTextStyle.merge(
              style: TextStyle(color: color == null ? Colors.black : Colors.white, fontWeight: FontWeight.bold),
              child: header,
            ),
          ),
          Padding(padding: const EdgeInsets.all(10), child: child),
          // no footer provided: no footer at all
          if (footer != null)
            Container(
              color: Colors.grey.shade100,
              padding: const EdgeInsets.all(8),
              child: DefaultTextStyle.merge(
                style: const TextStyle(color: Colors.grey, fontSize: 12),
                child: footer!,
              ),
            ),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • lines 18–21: Parameters: an optional color ([Color?]), and three slots for content: [header], [footer] (optional), and [child], the main content;
  • line 23: the header has default content: a constant widget;
  • line 27: the header color: the one provided, or light gray;
  • line 30: the colored header is cropped to match the card’s rounded corners;
  • lines 43–45: [DefaultTextStyle] sets the style of ALL the text in its subtree, regardless of the widget provided by the parent: the header is bold, white on a colored background;
  • line 48: the main content, provided by the parent;
  • lines 50–58: no footer provided; no footer at all. [footer!]: in this branch, [footer] is not [null] (the compiler cannot infer this for a field, hence the [!]).

docs.title: 4.3.2. A generic table
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex12_composition/simple_table.dart - a GENERIC table
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SimpleTable<T> is a generic widget: it displays rows of any
// type T. It knows how to go through the rows, but not how to display ONE
// row: the parent tells it, by passing it a FUNCTION,
// cells(row, index), which returns the widgets of the cells.
// It is the principle of Flutter's "builders" (ListView.builder,
// FutureBuilder...): the content provided by the parent uses data
// that belong to the child (the row, its rank).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

// the type of a function that builds the cells of a row
typedef CellsBuilder<T> = List<Widget> Function(T row, int index);

class SimpleTable<T> extends StatelessWidget {
  final List<T> rows;
  final List<String> columns;
  final CellsBuilder<T> cells;
  final Widget empty; // displayed when there is no row

  const SimpleTable({
    super.key,
    required this.rows,
    required this.columns,
    required this.cells,
    this.empty = const Text('No data.'),
  });

  // a cell: a little margin around its content
  static Widget _cell(Widget content) => Padding(padding: const EdgeInsets.all(6), child: content);

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    if (rows.isEmpty) {
      return Column(
        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
        children: [
          Text(columns.join('   '), style: const TextStyle(fontWeight: FontWeight.bold)),
          const Divider(),
          DefaultTextStyle.merge(
            style: const TextStyle(color: Colors.grey),
            child: empty,
          ),
        ],
      );
    }
    return Table(
      defaultVerticalAlignment: TableCellVerticalAlignment.middle,
      border: TableBorder(horizontalInside: BorderSide(color: Colors.grey.shade300)),
      children: [
        TableRow(
          children: [for (final c in columns) _cell(Text(c, style: const TextStyle(fontWeight: FontWeight.bold)))],
        ),
        for (final (i, row) in rows.indexed)
          // the cells of THIS row, built by the parent's function
          TableRow(children: [for (final c in cells(row, i)) _cell(c)]),
      ],
    );
  }
}
  • line 16: the type of a function that takes a row (of type [T]) and its index, and returns the widgets of its cells;
  • line 18: a generic widget: it displays rows of any type ([T]). It knows how to iterate through the rows, but not how to display ONE row; the parent tells it how by passing it the function [cells]. This is the principle behind [Flutter] “builders” ([ListView.builder], [FutureBuilder]...): the content is provided by the parent, but it uses data that belongs to the child (the line, its index). [React] calls this a “render prop”;
  • line 33: a [static] method, which does not use any fields from the widget;
  • lines 37–45: no row: the column headers and the [empty] content, provided by the parent;
  • lines 50–59: the table: a row of headers, followed by one row per line, whose cells are generated by the parent’s function.
